The three, the Kālakānjas, set aloft in heaven as they were Gods All these I call to be our help and keep this man secure from harm. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.81: A charm to facilitate child-birth
poems.excerpt:
Thou art a grasper, holding fast both hands: drivest fiends away.
A holder both of progeny and riches hath this Ring become.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.82: A charm to win a bride
poems.excerpt:
I call the name of him who comes, hath come, and still draws-nigh to us.
Foe-slaying Indra's name I love, the Vasus' friend with hundred powers.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.83: A charm against sores and pustules (apachitas)
poems.excerpt:
Hence, Sores and Pustules, fly away even as the eagle from his home.
Let Sūrya bring a remedy, the Moon shine forth and banish you.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.84: A charm to accompany the symbolical loosing of sacrificial victims
poems.excerpt:
Thou in whose dread mouth I present oblation, that these bound victims may obtain their freedom, The people deem that thou art Earth: I know thee thoroughly, and I say thou art Destruction.

Be thou enriched, O Welfare, with oblations, here among us is thine allotted portion. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.85: A charm against Consumption
poems.excerpt:
Let Varana the heavenly tree here present keep disease away.
The Gods have driven off Decline that entered and possessed this man.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.86: A glorification of a newly consecrated King
poems.excerpt:
This is the Lord of Indra, this the Lord of Heaven, the Lord of Earth, The Lord of all existing things: the one and only Lord be thou,

The Sea is regent of the floods, Agni is ruler of the land, The Moon is regent of the stars: the one and only Lord be thou. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.87: A benediction addressed to a newly elected King
poems.excerpt:
Here art thou: I have chosen thee. Stand stedfast and immov-able.
Let all the clans desire thee: let not thy kingdom fall away.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.88: A benediction addressed to a newly elected King
poems.excerpt:
Firm is the sky, firm is the earth, and firm is all this living world; Firm are these mountains on their base, and stedfast is this King of men.

Stedfast may Varuna the King, stedfast the God Brihaspati, Stedfast may Indra stedfast, too, may Agni keep thy stedfast reign. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.89: A man's love charm
poems.excerpt:
This strength that Soma hath bestowed, the head of her who gladdeneth,— With that which thence hath been produced we make thy spirit sorrowful.

We make thy spirit sorrowful, we fill thy mind with pain and grief. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.90: A charm to cure a poisoned man
poems.excerpt:
The shaft that Rudra hath shot forth against thy members and thy heart, Here do we draw from thee to-day, and turn it hence to every side.

From all the hundred vessels spread throughout the members of thy frame. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.91: A charm against disease
poems.excerpt:
They made this barley ready with a team of eight, a team of six.
With this I drive to westward, far away, thy bodily disease.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.92: A charm to strengthen and inspirit a war-horse
poems.excerpt:
Be fleet as wind, Strong Steed, when thou art harnessed; go forth as swift as thought at lndra's sending.
Let the possessors of all wealth, the Maruts, yoke thee, and Tvashtar in thy feet lay swiftness.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.93: A prayer for protection from poison
poems.excerpt:
Yama, Death direly fatal, the Destroyer, with his black crest, Sarva the tawny archer, And all the Gods uprisen with their army, may these on every side avoid our heroes.

With mind, burnt offerings, butter, and libation, to royal Bhava and the archer Sarva, To these the worshipful I pay my worship: may they turn else-where things with deadly venom. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.94: A charm to reconcile a King's discontented people
poems.excerpt:
We bend your minds in union, bend in harmony your hopes and plans: You there, who turn to sundered ways, we bend and bow in unison.

I with my spirit make your spirits captive: these with their thoughts follow my thought and wishes. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.95: A charm to remove disease
poems.excerpt:
In the third heaven above us stands the Asvattha tree, the seat of Gods.
There the Gods gained the Kushtha plant, embodiment of end-less life.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.96: A prayer for deliverance from sin and sorrow
poems.excerpt:
The many plants of hundred shapes and forms that Soma rules as King, Commanded by Brihaspati, deliver us from grief and woe!

Let them release me from the curse and from the noose of Varupa, Free me from Yama's fetter, and from every sin against the Gods! …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.98: Praise of Indra
poems.excerpt:
Indra be victor, never to be vanquished, to reign among the Kings as sovran ruler!
Here be thou meet for praise and supplication, to be revered and waited on and worshipped.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.99: A prayer for protection in battle
poems.excerpt:
Indra, before affliction comes, I call thee from the wide expanse.
The mighty guardian, born alone, wearer of many names, I call.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.100: A charm against poison
poems.excerpt:
The Gods and Sūrya gave the gift, the Earth and Heaven best-owed the boon.
The three Sarasvatis in full accord bestowed the antidote.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.101: A charm to promote virile vigour
poems.excerpt:
Taurum age, palpita, incresce et teipsum extende: per totum membrum increscat penis: hoc tu caede feminam.

Quo debilem stimulant, quo aegrum excitant (homines), hoc, O Brahmanaspatis, hujus penem in arcus modum extende. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.102: A man's love charm
poems.excerpt:
Even as this ox, O Asvins, steps and turns together with his mate, So let thy fancy turn itself, come nearer, and unite with me.

I, as the shaft-horse draws the mare beside him, draw thee to myself. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.103: A charm to check the approach of a hostile army
poems.excerpt:
Brihaspati and Savitar prepare a rope to bind you fast!
Let Bhaga, Mitra, Aryaman, and both the Asvins make the bond.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.104: The same
poems.excerpt:
We bind our foemen with a bond that binds them close and holds them fast.
Their breath and respiration I dissever, and their lives from life.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.105: A charm to cure cough
poems.excerpt:
Rapidly as the fancy flies forth with conceptions of the mind.
So following the fancy's flight, O Cough, flee rapidly away.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.106: A charm to protect a house from fire
poems.excerpt:
Let flowery Dūrvā grass grow up about thine exit and approach.
There let a spring of water rise, or lake with blooming lotuses.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.107: A charm to protect men and cattle
poems.excerpt:
Entrust me, Visvajit, to Trāyamānā.
Guard, Trāyamānā, all our men, guard all our wealth of quadrupeds.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.108: A prayer for wisdom
poems.excerpt:
Intelligence, come first to us with store of horses and of kine!
Thou with the rays of Sūrya art our worshipful and holy one.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.109: A charm to heal punctured wounds
poems.excerpt:
The Berry heals the missile's rent, it heals the deeply-piercing wound.
The Gods prepared and fashioned it. This hath sufficient power for life.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.110: A benediction on a new-born child
poems.excerpt:
Yea, ancient, meet for praise at sacrifices, ever and now thou sittest down as Hotar.
And now, O Agni, make thy person friendly, and win felicity for us by worship.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.111: A charm for insanity
poems.excerpt:
Unbind and loose for me this man, O Agni, who bound and well restrained is chattering folly.
Afterward he will offer thee thy portion when he hath been delivered from his madness.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.112: A health-charm for man, woman, and son
poems.excerpt:
Let not this one, O Agni, wound the highest of these: preserve thou him from utter ruin.
Knowing the way do thou untie the nooses of the she-fiend: let all the Gods approve thee.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.113: A charm to banish the fiend Grāhi
poems.excerpt:
This sin the Gods wiped off and laid on Trita, and Trita wiped it off on human beings.
Thence if the female fiend hath made thee captive, the Gods by prayer shall banish her and free thee.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.114: A prayer for pardon of faults and errors in sacrificing
poems.excerpt:
Whatever God-provoking wrong we priests have done, O Deities.
Therefrom do ye deliver us, Ādityas! by the right of Law.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.115: A prayer for forgiveness of sins
poems.excerpt:
Whatever wrong we wittingly or in our ignorance have done, Do ye deliver us therefrom, O all ye Gods, of one accord.

If I, a sinner, when awake or sleeping have committed sin, Free me therefrom as from a stake, from present and from future guilt. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.116: A prayer for pardon of sin against mother, father, son, or brother
poems.excerpt:
The wealth which husbandmen aforetime, digging, like men who find their food with knowledge, buried, This to the King, Vivasvān's son, I offer, Sweet be our food and fit for sacrificing!

May he, Vaivasvata, prepare our portion; May he whose share is mead with mead besprinkle. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.117: A prayer for freedom from debt
poems.excerpt:
That which I eat, a debt which still is owing, the tribute due to Yama, which supports me, Thereby may I be free from debt, O Agni. Thou knowest how to rend all bonds asunder.

Still dwelling here we give again this present; we send it forth, the living from the living. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.118: A prayer for pardon of cheating at play
poems.excerpt:
If we have sinned with both our hands, desiring to take the host of dice for our possession, May both Apsarases to-day forgive us that debt, the fiercely-conquering, fiercely-looking.

Stern viewers of their sins who rule the people, forgive us what hash happened as we gambled. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.119: A prayer for release from debts incurred without intention of payment
poems.excerpt:
The debt which I incur, not gaming, Agni! and, not intending to repay, acknowledge, That may Vaisvānara, the best, our sovran, carry away into the world of virtue.

I cause Vaisvānara to know, confessing the debt whose payment to the Gods is promised. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.120: A prayer for pardon of sins and felicity hereafter
poems.excerpt:
If we have injured Air, or Earth, or Heaven, if we have wronged our Mother or our Father, May Agni Gārhapatya here absolve us, and bear us up into the world of virtue.

Earth is our Mother, Aditi our birth-place: our brother Air save us from imprecation! …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.121: A prayer for happiness in heaven
poems.excerpt:
Spreading them out, untie the snares that hold us, Varuna's bonds, the upper and the lower.
Drive from us evil dream, drive off misfortune; then let us go in-to the world of virtue.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.122: A prayer for happiness in heaven
poems.excerpt:
This portion I who understand deliver to Visvakarman first-born son of Order.
So may we follow to the end, unbroken, beyond old age, the thread which we have given.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.123: A prayer for happiness in heaven
poems.excerpt:
Ye who are present, unto you I offer this treasure brought to us by Jātavedas Happily will the sacrificer follow: do ye acknowledge him in highest heaven.

Do ye acknowledge him in highest heaven: ye know the world here present in assembly. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.124: An Omen from the sky
poems.excerpt:
From the high firmament, yea, out of heaven a water-drop with dew on me hath fallen.
I, Agni! share the merit of the pious, with vigour, milk, and hymns and sacrifices.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.125: Glorification of a war-chariot
poems.excerpt:
Mayst thou, O Tree, be firm indeed in body, our friend that furthers us, a goodly hero.
Put forth thy strength, compact with thongs of leather, and let thy rider win all spoils of battle.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.126: Glorification of the war drum
poems.excerpt:
Send forth thy voice aloud through earth and heaven, and let the world in all its breadth regard thee.
O Drum, accordant with the Gods and Indra, drive thou afar, yea, very far, our foemen.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.127: A charm to banish various diseases
poems.excerpt:
Of abscess, of decline, of inflammation of the eyes. O Plant, Of penetrating pain, thou Herb, let not a particle remain.

Those nerves of thine, Consumption! which stand closely hidden in thy groin I know the balm for that disease: the magic cure is Sipudru. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.128: A charm for fair weather
poems.excerpt:
What time the heavenly bodies chose the Weather Prophet as their King, They brought him favouring weather, and, Let this be his do-main, they said.

May we have weather fair at noon, May we have weather fair at eve, Fair weather when the morning breaks, fair weather when the night is come. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.129: A charm for success and happiness
poems.excerpt:
With fortune of the Sisu tree—with Indra as my friend to aid I give myself a happy fate. Fly and begone, Malignities!

That splendour and felicity wherewith thou hast excelled the trees Give me therewith a happy fate. Fly and begone, Malignities …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.130: A woman's love-charm
poems.excerpt:
This is the Apsarases' love-spell, the conquering, resistless ones'.
Send the spell forth, ye Deities! Let him consume with love of me.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.131: A woman's love-charm
poems.excerpt:
Down upon thee, from head to foot, I draw the pangs of long-ing love.
Send forth the charm, ye Deities! Let him consume with love of me.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.132: The same
poems.excerpt:
The Philter, burning with the pangs of yearning love, which Gods have poured within the bosom of the floods, That spell for thee I heat by Varuna's decree.

The charm which, burning with the pangs of love, the General Gods have poured within the bosom of the floods, That spell for thee I heat by Varuna's decree. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.133: A glorification of the sacred girdle
poems.excerpt:
By the direction of that God we journey, he will seek means to save and he will free us; The God who hath engirt us with this Girdle, he who hath fast-ened it, and made us ready.

Thou, weapon of the Rishis, art adored and served with sacrifice. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.134: A priest's prayer for power to punish wrong-doers
poems.excerpt:
This Thunderbolt shall take its fill of Order, scare life away and overthrow the kingdom.
Tear necks in pieces. rend napes asunder, even as the Lord of Might the neck of Vritra.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.135: A priest's fulmination against an enemy
poems.excerpt:
Whate'er I eat I turn to strength, and thus I grasp the Thunder-bolt, Rending the shoulders of that man as Indra shattered Vritra's neck.

I drink together what I drink, even as the sea that swallows all. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.136: A charm to promote the growth of hair
poems.excerpt:
Born from the bosom of wide Earth the Goddess, godlike Plant, art thou: So we, Nitatnī! dig thee up to strengthen and fix fast the hair.

Make the old firm, make new hair spring, lengthen what has already grown. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.137: A charm to promote the growth of hair
poems.excerpt:
The Plant which Jamadagni dug to make his daughter's locks.
grow long, This same hath Vitahavya brought to us from Asita's abode.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.138: A woman's imprecation on her unfaithful lover
poems.excerpt:
O Plant, thy fame is spread abroad as best of all the herbs that grow.
Unman for me to-day this man that he may wear the horn of hair.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.139: A woman's love-charm
poems.excerpt:
Thou hast grown up, a source of joy to bless me with pros-perity.
A hundred are thy tendrils, three-and-thirty thy descending shoots.
With this that bears a thousand leaves I dry thy heart and wither it. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.140: A blessing on a child's first two teeth
poems.excerpt:
Two tigers have grown up who long to eat the mother and the sire: Soothe, Brāhmanaspati, and thou, O Jātavedas, both these teeth.

Let rice and barley be your food, eat also beans and sesamum. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.141: A blessing on cattle
poems.excerpt:
Vayu collected these: to find their sustenance be Tvashtar's care: May Indra bless and comfort them, and Rudra look that they increase.

Take thou the iron axe and make a pair by marks upon their ears. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 6.142: A blessing on cattle
poems.excerpt:
Spring high, O Barley, and become much through thine own magnificence: Burst all the vessels; let the bolt from heaven forbear to strike thee down.

As we invite and call to thee, Barley, a God who heareth us, Raise thyself up like heaven on high and be exhaustless as the sea. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.1: Glorification of the power of prayer and to Agni
poems.excerpt:
They who by thought have guided all that Speech hath best, or they who with their heart have uttered words of truth, Made stronger by the strength which the third prayer bestows, have by the fourth prayer learned the nature of the Cow.

Well knows this son his sire, he knows his mother well: he hath been son, and he hath been illiberal. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.2: Praise of Atharvan
poems.excerpt: Invoke for us, proclaim in sundry places, the kinsman of the Gods, our sire Atharvan, His mother's germ, his father's breath, the youthful, who with his mind hath noticed this oblation.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.3: To Vāyu God of the Wind
poems.excerpt: With thine eleven teams, to aid our wishes, yea, with thy two-and-twenty teams, O Vāyu, With all thy three-and-thirty teams for drawing, here loose these teams, thou who art prompt to listen!

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.5: A glorification of sacrifice
poems.excerpt:
The Gods adored the Sacrifice with worship: these were the statutes of primeval ages.
Those mighty ones attained the cope of heaven, there where the Sādhyas, Gods of old, are dwelling.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.7: Praise of the Ādityas
poems.excerpt:
I have sung praise to Diti's sons and Aditi's, those very lofty and invulnerable Gods.
For far within the depths of ocean is their home and in the wor-ship paid them none excelleth these.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.8: Godspeed to a departing traveller
poems.excerpt:
Go forward on thy way from good to better: Brihaspati pre-cede thy steps and guide thee!
Place this man here, within this earth's enclosure, afar from foes with all his men about him.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.9: A prayer to Pūshan for protection and the recovery of lost property
poems.excerpt:
Pūshan was born to move on distant pathways, on roads remote from earth, remote from heaven.
To both most lovely places of assembly he travels and returns with perfect knowledge.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.10: A prayer for the favour of Sarasvati
poems.excerpt:
That breast of thine, exhaustless and delightful, good to invoke, beneficent, free giver.
Wherewith thou feedest all things that are choicest, bring that, Sarasvati, that we may drain it.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.11: A prayer to protect corn from lightning and drought
poems.excerpt: That far-spread thunder, sent from thee, which cometh on all this world, a high celestial signal Strike not, O God, our growing corn with lightning, not kill it with the burning rays of Sūrya.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.12: A prayer for influence at deliberative and religious meetings
poems.excerpt:
In concord may Prajapati's two daughters, Gathering and As-sembly, both protect me.
May every man I meet respect and aid me. Fair be my words, O Fathers, at the meetings.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.13: A charm to win superiority over foes and rivals
poems.excerpt:
As the Sun, rising, taketh to himself the brightness of the stars,.
So I assume the glory of women and men mine enemies.
All ye amang my rivals who behold me as I come to you, I seize the glory of my foes as the Sun, rising, theirs who sleep.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.14: A prayer to Savitar for prosperity
poems.excerpt:
I praise this God, parent of heaven and earth, exceeding wiser possessed of real energy, giver of treasure, thinker dear to all,.

Whose splendour is sublime, whose light shone brilliant in crea-tion, who, wise, and golden-handed, in his beauty made the sky. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.15: A charm to win divine favour and felicity
poems.excerpt: I choose, O Savitar, that glorious favour, with fruitful energy and every blessing, Even this one's teeming cow, erst milked by Kanva, thousand-streamed, milked for happiness by the mighty.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.16: A prayer for prosperity
poems.excerpt:
Increase this man Brihaspati! Illume him, O Savitar, for high and happy fortune.
Sharpen him thoroughly though already sharpened: with glad acclaim let all the Gods receive him.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.17: A prayer for wealth and children
poems.excerpt:
May the Ordainer give us wealth, Lord, ruler of the world of life: with full hand may he give to us.

May Dhātar grant the worshipper henceforth imperishable life. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.18: A prayer for rain
poems.excerpt:
Burst open, Prithvi, and cleave asunder this celestial cloud.
Untie, O Dhātar—for thou canst—the bottle of the breast of heaven.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.19: A prayer for prosperity
poems.excerpt:
Prajapati engenders earthly creatures: may the benevolent Ordainer form them, Having one common womb, and mind, and spirit. He who is.
Lord of Plenty give me plenty!

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.20: A prayer for prosperity and happiness
poems.excerpt:
Anumati approve to-day our sacrifice among the Gods!
May Agni bear mine offerings away for me the worshipper.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.21: A funeral stanza
poems.excerpt:
With prayer come all together to the Lord of Heaven: he is the peerless one, far-reaching, guest of men.
He, God of ancient time, hath gained a recent thrall; to him alone is turned the path which all must tread.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.22: To Savitar, or Yama invested with Savitar's attributes
poems.excerpt:
Unto a thousand sages he hath given sight: thought, light is he in ranging all.

The Bright One hath sent forth the Dawns, a closely gathered band, Immaculate, unanimous, brightly refulgent in their homes.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.23: A charm to banish fiends and troubles
poems.excerpt:
The fearful dream, and indigence, the monster, the malignant hags.
All female fiends of evil name and wicked tongue we drive afar.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.24: A prayer for riches
poems.excerpt: What treasure hath been dug for us by Indra, by Agni, Visve-devas, tuneful Maruts, On us may Savitar whose laws are faithful, Prajāpati, and Heavenly Grace bestow it.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.25: Praise of Vishnu and Varuna
poems.excerpt:
The early morning prayer hath come to Vishnu and Varuna, Lords through might, whom none hath equalled, Gods by whose power the realms of air were stablished, strongest and most heroic in their vigour.

The early prayer hath ever come to Vishnu and Varuna by that God's high power and statute. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.26: Praise of Vishnu
poems.excerpt:
I will declare the mighty deeds of Vishnu, of him who measured out the earthly regions, Who propped the highest place of congregation, thrice setting down his footstep, widely striding.

Loud boast doth Vishnu make of this achievement, like some wild beast, dread, prowling, mountain-roaming. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.27: A prayer to Ida, Goddess of devotion
poems.excerpt:
May Idā with her statute dwell beside us, she in whose place the pious purge and cleanse them.
She, mighty, Soma-decked, whose foot drops fatness, meet for All-Gods, hath come to aid our worship.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.28: Praise of the sacrificial utensils
poems.excerpt:
Blest be the Broom, may the Mace bring a blessing, and may the Altar and the Hatchet bless us.
Worshipful Gods, may they accept this worship, lovers of sacri-fice, and sacrificers.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.29: To Agni and Vishnu
poems.excerpt:
This is your glorious might, Agni and Vishnu! Ye drink the essence of the mystic butter.
Placing in every home seven costly treasures. Let your tongue stretch to take the offered fatness.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.30: A charm to be used when the eyes are anointed
poems.excerpt: Heaven, Earth, and Mitra here have caused mine eyes to be-anointed well, Savitar, Brāhmanaspati take care that they be duly balmed!

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.31: A prayer for the overthrow of enemies
poems.excerpt: Rouse us to-day O Indra, Maghavan, hero, with thy best pos-sible and varied succours, May he who hateth us fall low beneath us, and him whom we detest let life abandon.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.32: A prayer to Agni for long life
poems.excerpt: We bringing homage have approached the friend who seeks our wondering praise, Young, strengthener of the sacrifice. May he bestow long life on me.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.33: A prayer for long life, children, and riches
poems.excerpt:
Let Pūshan, let the Maruts, let Brihaspati pour forth on me; This present Agni pour on me children and riches in a stream!
May he bestow long life on me.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.34: A prayer for freedom from sin and the overthrow of enemies
poems.excerpt:
Agni, drive off my rivals born and living, repel those yet unborn, O Jātavedas.
Cast down beneath my feet mine adversaries. In Aditi's regard may we be sinless.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.35: A prayer for the prosperity of a King and his kingdom
poems.excerpt:
Subdue with conquering might his other rivals, those yet unborn repel, O Jātavedas.
For great felicity protect this kingdom, and in this man let all the Gods be joyful.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.36: A charm to be pronounced by bride and bridegroom
poems.excerpt: Sweet are the glances of our eyes, our faces are as smooth as balm, Within thy bosom harbour me; one spirit dwell in both of us!

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.37: A nuptial charm to be spoken by the bride
poems.excerpt: With this my robe, inherited from Manu, I envelop thee, So that thou mayst be all mine own and give no thought to other dames.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.38: A maiden's love-charm
poems.excerpt:
I dig this Healing Herb that makes my lover look on me and weep; That bids the parting friend return and kindly greets him as he comes.

This Herb wherewith the Asuri drew Indra downward from the Gods, With this same Herb I draw thee close that I may be most dear to thee. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.39: A sacrificial charm for rain and prosperity
poems.excerpt: May he establish in our home the master of riches, gladdening with rain in season, Mighty, strong-winged, celestial, dropping moisture, Bull of the plants and embryo of waters.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.40: A prayer for prosperity
poems.excerpt:
We call Sarasvān, under whose protection all cattle wander, to preserve and aid us, Him in whose ordinance abide the waters, to whose command the Lord of Plenty listens.

Abiding here let us invoke Sarasvān, the seat of riches, glorious, wealth-increaser, Him who inclines and gives to him who worships, the rich pos-sessor and the Lord of Fulness.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.41: A prayer for prosperity
poems.excerpt:
Observing men, and viewing home, the Falcon hath cleft his swift way over wastes and waters.
May he, with Indra for a friend, auspicious, traversing all air's lower realms, come hither.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.42: A prayer for delivery from sin and sickness
poems.excerpt:
Scatter and drive away, Soma and Rudra, the sickness that hath come within our dwelling, Afar into the distance chase Destruction, and even from commit-ted sin release us.

Lay on our bodies, O ye twain, O Soma and Rudra, all those balms that heal diseases. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.43: A charm against lightning
poems.excerpt:
Some of thy words bode weal and some misfortune: thou scat-terest them all with friendly feeling.
Deep within this three words are laid: among them one hath flown off even as the sound was uttered.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.44: In praise of Indra and Vishnu
poems.excerpt:
Ye twain have conquered, and have not been vanquished: not either of the pair hath been defeated.
Ye, Indra Vishnu, when ye fought your battle; produced this infinite with three divisions.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.45: A charm against jealousy
poems.excerpt:
Brought hitherward from Sindhu, from a folk of every mingled race, Fetched from afar, thou art I deem, a balm that cureth.
jealousy.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.46: A charm for offspring and prosperity
poems.excerpt:
O broad-tressed Sinivāli, thou who art the sister of the Gods, Accept the offered sacrifice, and, Goddess, grant us progeny.

Present the sacrifice to her, to Sinivāli, Queen of men, Beauti-ful-fingered, lovely-armed, prolific, bearing many a child. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.47: A prayer for wealth and birth of a son
poems.excerpt:
Oft in this sacrifice with favoured cry I call Kuhū, beneficent Goddess, skilled in all her works.
May she vouchsafe us wealth with every boon, and give a, hero meet for praise who gives a hundred gifts.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.48: A prayer for prosperity and the birth of a son
poems.excerpt:
I call on Rākā with hair laud and reverent cry: may she, auspicious, hear us and herself observe.
With never-breaking needle may she sew her work, and send a glorious man who gives a hundred gifts.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.49: A prayer for children and booty
poems.excerpt:
May the Gods' Consorts aid us of their own free will, help us to offspring and the winning of the spoil.
May Goddesses who quickly listen shelter us, both those on earth and they within the waters' realm.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.50: A gambler's prayer for success in gaming
poems.excerpt:
As evermore the lightning flash strikes, irresistible, the tree, So, irresistible, may I conquer the gamblers with the dice.

From every side, from hale and sick, impotent to defend them-selves, May all the fortune of the folk as winnings pass into my hands. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.51: A prayer for Brihaspati's and Indra's protection
poems.excerpt:
Brihaspati protect us from the sinner, from rearward, from above, and from below us!
May Indra from the front and from the centre, as friend to friends, vouchsafe us room and freedom.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.52: A prayer for peace and concord
poems.excerpt:
Give us agreement with our own, with strangers give us unity: Do ye, O Asvins, in this place join us in sympathy and love.

May we agree in mind, agree in purpose: let us not fight against the heavenly spirit. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.53: A charm to recover a sick man at the point of death
poems.excerpt:
As thou, Brihaspati, from the curse hast saved us, from dwel-ling yonder in the realm of Yama, The Asvins, leeches of the Gods, O Agni, have chased Death far from us with mighty powers.

Move both together; do not leave the body. Let both the breathings stay for thee united. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.54: A charm to obtain knowledge of the Veda
poems.excerpt:
We worship holy Verse and Song, by which they carry out their acts, Shining in order's seat these twain present the sacrifice to Gods.

As I have asked about Verse, Song, Sacrifice, strength, force,. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.55: A charm to ensure a prosperous journey
poems.excerpt: Thy downward paths from heaven, whereby thou hast raised all the world to life, Give us in gracious love, good Lord!

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.56: A charm against poisonous bites and stings
poems.excerpt:
Whether it came from viper, from black snake or snake with transverse stripes, Or Kankaparvan's bite, this herb hath made the poison power-less.

Honey-born, honey-dropping, rich in honey, honeysweet, this herb, Is medicine that heals the wound and kills the gnat that bites and stings. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.57: A charm for some physical disorder
poems.excerpt:
Whatever trouble hath disturbed and shaken me—I speak with hope, I move, imploring, 'mid the folk What harm my body in myself hath suffered, now let Sarasvati relieve with fatness.

Seven flow for him, the youth on whom the Maruts wait: the sons have taught the Father everlasting laws. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.58: An invitation to Indra and Varuna
poems.excerpt:
True to laws, Indra Varuna, drinkers of the juice, quaff this pressed Soma which shall give you rapturous joy!
Let sacrifice, your car, to entertain the Gods, approach its rest-ing-place that they may drink thereof.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.59: An imprecation
poems.excerpt:
Like a tree struck by lightning may the man be withered from the root.
Who curseth us who curse not him, or, when we curse him.
curseth us.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.60: A parting traveller's address to the houses of his village
poems.excerpt:
I, prudent, bringing power, a treasure-winner, with amicable eye that strikes no terror, Come, praising and kind-thoughted, to these houses: be not afraid of me, be glad and joyful.

Let these delightful Houses that are rich in power and store of milk, Replete with wealth and standing firm, become aware of our approach. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.61: A prayer for sacred knowledge and its fruits
poems.excerpt:
Since, Agni, with our fervent zeal we undergo austerity, May we be dear to Sacred Lore, may we be wise and live long lives.

Agni, we practise acts austere, we undergo austerity. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.62: A prayer for the overthrow of enemies
poems.excerpt:
Like a car-warrior, Agni here, grown mighty, Lord of the brave, Chief Priest, hath conquered footmen.
Laid on earth's centre he hath flashed and glittered. Low may he lay our enemies beneath us.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.63: A prayer for deliverance from affliction
poems.excerpt:
We call with lauds from his most lofty dwelling victorious Agni, conqueror in battles.
May he conveyus over all distresses, may the God Agni bear us past our troubles.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.64: A charm to avert an evil omen
poems.excerpt:
From all that woe and trouble may the Waters save and rescue me, Whate'er the Raven, black of hue, flying out hither ward, hath dropped.

May Agni Gārhapatya save and set me free from all this guilt. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.65: A charm against imprecation and threatened evils
poems.excerpt:
With retroverted fruit hast thou, O Apāmārga, sprung and grown.
Hence into distance most remote drive every curse away from, me.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.66: A prayer to Vāk
poems.excerpt:
If it was in the wind or air's mid-region, if it was in the trees or in the bushes, To meet whose utterance forth streamed the cattle, may that.
Celestial Power again approach us.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.67: A priest's prayer to the Agnayo Dhishnyāh
poems.excerpt:
May sense return to me again, and spirit, return my Sacred Power and my possessions!
Again let fires, aflame on lesser altars, each duly stationed, here succeed and prosper.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.68: A prayer for children and prosperity
poems.excerpt:
Sarasvati, in thy decrees, Goddess, in thy celestial laws, Accept the offered sacrifice, and, Goddess, grant us progeny.

Here is, Sarasvati, thy fat libation, this sacrifice passing to the mouth of Fathers. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.69: A prayer for prosperity
poems.excerpt:
May the wind kindly breathe on us, may the Sun warm us.
pleasantly.
May days pass happily for us, may night draw near delightfully, may dawn break joyfully for us!

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.70: A charm to frustrate an enemy's sacrifice
poems.excerpt:
Whatever sacrifice that man performeth with voice, mind, sacred formula, oblation, May, in accord with Death, Destruction ruin his offering before it gain fulfilment.

For him may sorcerers, Destruction, demons strike and prevent fulfilment through their falsehood. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.71: In praise of Agni
poems.excerpt: We set thee round us as a fort, victorious Agni! thee a sage, Bold in thy colour day by day, destroyer of the treacherous foe.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.72: An invitation to Indra
poems.excerpt:
Rise up and look upon the share of Indra fixt by ritual use.
Whether ye poured libation dressed or took delight in it un-cooked.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.73: An invitation to the Asvins
poems.excerpt:
Inflamed is Agni, Heroes! charioteer of heaven. The caldron boils: the meath is drained to be your food.
For we, O Asvins, singers sprung from many a house, invite you to be present at our banquetings.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.74: A charm to cure pustules, sores, or scrofulous swellings (apachitas)
poems.excerpt:
Black is the mother, we have heard, from whom the red-hued Pustules sprang.
With the divine ascetic's root I pierce and penetrate them all.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.75: A blessing on cows
poems.excerpt:
Let not a thief or wicked man possess you: let not the dart of Rudra come anear you, Prolific, shining in the goodly pasture, drinking at pleasant pools the limpid water.

Ye know the place and rest content, close-gathered, called by many a name. Come to me, Goddesses, with Gods Bedew with streams of fatness us, this cattle-pen, and all this place.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.76: A charm to cure scrofulous pustules and scrofula
poems.excerpt:
Rapidly dropping, quick to drop, more evil than the evil ones, More sapless than a dried-up bone, swifter than salt to melt away.

Pustules that rise upon the neck, Pustules upon the shoulder-joints, Pustules that, falling of themselves, spring up on every twofold limb: …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.77: An incantation against an enemy
poems.excerpt:
Ye Maruts, full of fiery heat, accept this offering brought for you To help us, ye who slay the foe.

Maruts, the man who filled with rage against us beyond our thoughts would harm us, O ye Vasus, May he be tangled in the toils of Mischief: smite ye him down with your most flaming weapon. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.78: A charm for a prince's prosperity
poems.excerpt:
I free thee from the cord, I loose the bond, I loose the fastening.
Even here, perpetual, Agni, wax thou strong.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.79: A hymn to the New Moon
poems.excerpt:
Night of the New-born Moon, whatever fortune the Gods who dwell with greatness have assigned thee, Therewith fulfil our sacrifice, all-baunteous! Blessed One, grant us wealth with manly offspring.

I am the New Moon's Night, the good and pious are my in-habitants, these dwell within me. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.80: A hymn to the Full Moon
poems.excerpt:
Full in the front, full rearward, from the middle the Full Moon's Night hath conquered in the battle.
In her: may we, dwelling with Gods and greatness, feast in the height of heaven, on strengthening viands.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.81: A hymn to the New Moon
poems.excerpt:
Forward and backward by their wondrous power move these two youths, disporting, round the ocean.
One views all living things, and thou, the other, art born again arranging times and seasons.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.82: In praise of Agni
poems.excerpt:
Sing with fair laud the combat for the cattle. Bestow upon us excellent possessions.
Lead to the Gods the sacrifice we offer: let streams of oil flow pure and full of sweetness.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.83: A prayer for deliverance from sin and other evils
poems.excerpt:
Stablished amid the waters is, King Varuna, thy golden home.
Thence let the Sovran who maintains the statutes loose all bind-ing cords.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.84: A prayer for protection
poems.excerpt:
Holder of sway, shine here refulgent, Agni! invincible immortal Jātavedas.
With succours friendly to mankind, auspicious, driving away all maladies, guard our dwelling.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.85: A charm to ensure victory in battle
poems.excerpt: This very mighty one whom Gods urge onward, the conqueror of cars, ever triumphant, Swift, fleet to battle, with uninjured fellies, even Tārkshya for our weal will we call hither.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.86: The same
poems.excerpt: Indra the rescuer, Indra the helper, Indra the brave who hears each invocation, Sakra I call, Indra invoked of many. May Indra Maghavan pros-per and bless us.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.87: A prayer to Rudra as Agni
poems.excerpt: To Rudra in the fire, to him who dwells in floods, to Rudra who hath entered into herbs and plants, To him who formed and fashioned all these worlds, to him this Rudra, yea, to Agni, reverence be paid!

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.88: A charm to cure a snake-bite
poems.excerpt:
Depart! thou art a foe, a foe. Poison with poison hast thou mixt, yea, verily poison hast thou mixt.
Go to the serpent: strike him dead.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.89: A prayer for purification and prosperity
poems.excerpt:
The heavenly Waters have I ranged: we have been sated with their dew.
Here, Agni, bearing milk, am I. Endow me with the gift of strength.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.90: A charm against a rival in love
poems.excerpt:
Tear thou asunder, as of old, like tangles of a creeping plant.
Demolish thou the Dāsa's might.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.91: A Prayer for protection
poems.excerpt:
May Indra with his help, Lord of all treasures, be unto us a careful protector.
Drive off our foes and give us peace and safety. May we be lords of goodly store of heroes.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.92: A Prayer for protection
poems.excerpt:
May this rich Indra as our good protector keep even far away the men who hate us.
May we enjoy his favour, his the holy: may we enjoy his blessed loving-kindness.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.93: A prayer for success in battle
poems.excerpt: With Indra's and with Manyu's aid may we subdue our enemies, resistlessly destroying foes.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.94: A charm to ensure the obedience of subjects
poems.excerpt: We laid the constant Soma on with constant sacrificial gift, That Indra may make all the tribes unanimous and only ours.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.95: An incantation against an undetected thief
poems.excerpt:
To heaven, as 'twere, have soared this man's two vultures, staggering, dusky hued.
The Parcher and the Drier-up, the pair who parch and dry his heart.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.96: An incantation against an undetected thief
poems.excerpt: The kine are resting in the stall, home to her nest hath flown the bird, The hills are firmly rooted: I have fixed the kidneys in their place.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.97: Sacrificial formulas
poems.excerpt:
As we have here elected thee, skilled Hotar! to-day as this our sacrifice proceedeth, Come to the firm place, mightiest! yea, come firmly. Knowing the sacrifice, approach the Soma.

With kine connect us, and with spirit, Indra! Lord of Bay Steeds, with princes and with favour, With the God-destined portion of the Brāhmans, and the good-will of Gods who merit worship. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.98: Anointing the sacred grass
poems.excerpt:
Balmed is the Grass with butter and libation, with Indra.
gracious Lord, and with the Maruts.
Hail! let the sacrifice go forth anointed to Indra with the Gods and Visve Devas.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.99: The preparation of the altar
poems.excerpt:
Strew thou the Grass, and spread it on the Altar: rob not the sister who is lying yonder.
The Hotar's seat is green and golden: these are gold necklets.
in the plaee of him who worships.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.100: A charm against nightmare
poems.excerpt:
I turn away from evil dream, from dream of sin, from indigence.
I make the prayer mine inmost friend. Hence! torturing.
dreamy phantasies!

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.101: The same
poems.excerpt:
The food that in a dream I eat is not perceived at early morn.
May all that food be blest to me because it is not seen by day.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.102: A charm to obtain pardon for an indecent act
poems.excerpt: When I have worshipped Heaven and Earth, reverenced Firma-ment and Death, I will make water standing up. Let not the Sovrans injure me.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.103: The cry of an unemployed priest
poems.excerpt:
What princely warrior, seeking higher fortune, will free us from this shameful fiend of mischief?
What friend of sacrifice? What guerdon-lover? Who winneth: 'mid the Gods a long existence?

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.104: A prayer for prosperity
poems.excerpt: Who will prepare the dappled Cow, good milker, ne'er without calf, whom Varuna gave Atharvan, And, joying in Brihaspati's alliance, arrange according to his will her body?

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.105: An initiation formula
poems.excerpt: Leaving humanity behind, making the heavenly word thy choice, With all thy friends address thyself to furthering and guiding men.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.106: A prayer for pardon of sin
poems.excerpt:
Each thoughtless ill that we have done, O Agni, all error in our conduct, Jātavedas!
Therefrom do thou, O sapient God, preserve us. May we thy friends, for bliss, have life eternal.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.107: A charm against Cough
poems.excerpt: The seven bright beams of Surya bring the waters downward from the sky, The streams of ocean: these have made the sting that pained thee drop away.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.108: A prayer for protection
poems.excerpt:
Whoso by stealth or openly would harm us, a friend who knows us, or a stranger, Agni!
May the strange she-fiend armed with teeth attack them: O Agni, theirs be neither home nor children!
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.109: A prayer for success in gambling
poems.excerpt:
My homage to the strong, the brown, the sovran lord among the dice!
Butter on Kali I bestow: may he be kind to one like me.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.110: A prayer for success in battle
poems.excerpt:
Resistless, Agni, Indra, smite his foemen for the worshipper, For best foe-slayers are ye both.

Agni I call, and Indra, foe-destroyers, swift moving, heroes, Gods who wield the thunder, Through whom they won the light in the beginning, these who have made all worlds their habitation. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.111: A prayer for offspring
poems.excerpt:
Belly of Indra art thou, Soma-holder! the very soul of Gods and human beings.
Here be the sire of offspring, thine here present! Here be they glad in thee who now are elsewhere.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.112: A prayer for protection and freedom from sin
Atharva Veda 7.113: A woman's incantation against a rival
poems.excerpt:
Rough Plant, thou rough rude parasite, cut thou that man, O Rough and Rude, That thou mayst hinder from his act that man in all his manly strength.

Thou, rugged Plant, art rude and rough, Vishā, Vishātaki art thou. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.114: A woman's incantation against a rival
poems.excerpt:
I have extracted from thy sides, I have extracted from thy heart, I have extracted from thy face the strength and splendour that were thine.

Let pain and suffering pass away, let cares and curses vanish. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.115: A charm against Misfortune
poems.excerpt:
Hence. Evil Fortune! fly away, vanish from this place and from that.
We fix thee with an iron hook unto the man who hateth us.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.116: A charm against Fever
poems.excerpt:
Homage to him the burning one, shaker, exciter, violent!
Homage to him the cold who acts according to his ancient will!
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.117: A charm to ensure prosperity
poems.excerpt:
Come hither, Indra, with bay steeds, joyous, with tails like pea-cock plumes.
Let none impede thy way as fowlers stay the bird: pass o'er them as o'er desert lands.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 7.118: A benediction on a warrior
poems.excerpt:
Thy vital parts I cover with thine armour: with immortality King Soma clothe thee!
Varuna give thee what is more than ample, and in thy triumph let the Gods be joyful.

poems.title: Atharva Veda 8.1: A charm to recover a dying man
poems.excerpt:
Homage to Death the Ender! May thy breathings, inward and outward, still remain within thee.
Here stay this man united with his spirit in the Sun's realm, the world of life eternal!
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 8.2: The same
poems.excerpt:
Seize to thyself this trust of life for ever: thine be longevity which nothing shortens.
Thy spirit and thy life again I bring thee: die not, nor vanish into mist and darkness.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 8.3: A prayer for the destruction of demons
poems.excerpt:
I balm with oil the mighty demon-slayer, to the most famous friend I come for shelter.
Enkindled, sharpened by our rites, may Agni protect us in the day and night from evil.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 8.4: Imprecations on demons
poems.excerpt:
Indra and Soma, burn, destroy the demon foe! Send downward, O ye Bulls, those who add gloom to gloom.
Annihilate the fools, slay them and burn them up: chase them away from us, pierce the voracious fiends.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 8.5: A charm accompanying investiture with an amulet
poems.excerpt:
Upon the strong is bound the strong, this magic cord, this Amu-let, Potent, foe-slayer, served by valiant heroes, happy and fortu-nate defence.

This Charm, foe-slayer, served by many heroes, strong, power-ful, victorious, and mighty, goes bravely forth to meet and ruin witchcraft. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 8.6: A charm to exercise evil spirits who beset women
poems.excerpt:
Let neither fiend of evil name, Alinsa, Vatsapa, desire Thy pair of husband-wooers which thy mother cleansed when, thou wast born.

Palala, Anupalala, Sarku, Koka, Malimlucha, Palijaka Vavri-vāsas and Asresha, Rikshagriva and Pramilin. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 8.7: A charm to restore a sick man to health
poems.excerpt:
The tawny-coloured, and the pale, the variegated and the red, The dusky-tinted, and the black,—all Plants we summon hither-ward.

This man let them deliver from Consumption which the Gods have sent. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 8.8: Imprecations directed against a hostile army
poems.excerpt:
Indra the Shaker shake them up, brave, hero, fortdemolisher, That into thousand fragments we may strike the armies of our foes!

Let Pūtirajju with her breath corrupt and putrefy that host, And terror smite our foemen's heart when fire and smoke are seen afar. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 8.9: An enunciation of cosmogonical, ritual, and metrical doctrine
poems.excerpt:
Whence were these two produced? which was that region?'
From what world, from which earth had they their being?
Calves of Virāj, these two arose from water. I ask thee of these twain, who was their milker. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 8.10: A glorification of the mystical abstraction Virāj
poems.excerpt:
Viraj at first was This. At birth all feared her; the thought, She will become this All, struck terror.

She rose, the Gārhapatya fire she entered. He who knows this becomes lord of a household, performer of domestic sacri-fices. …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 9.1: A glorification of the Asvins' whip and a prayer for blessings
poems.excerpt:
The Asvins' Honey-whip was born from heaven and earth, from middle air, and ocean, and from fire and wind.
All living creatures welcome it with joyful hearts, fraught with the store of Amrit it hath gathered up.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 9.2: A glorification of Kāma as God of desire of all that is good
poems.excerpt:
Kāma the Bull, slayer of foes, I worship with molten butter, sacrifice, oblation.
Beneath my feet cast down mine adversaries with thy great manly power, when I have praised thee.
 …

poems.title: Atharva Veda 9.3: On the consecration of a newly built house
poems.excerpt:

poems.excerpt:
Here I begin: and first I pray the choir of the Muses to come down from Helicon into my heart to aid the lay which I have newly written in tablets upon my knee. Fain would I sound in all men’s ears that awful strife, that clamorous deed of war, and tell how the Mice proved their valour on the Frogs and rivalled the exploits of the Giants, those earth-born men, as the tale was told among mortals. Thus did the war begin.

One day a thirsty Mouse who had escaped the ferret, dangerous foe, set his soft muzzle to the lake’s brink and revelled in the sweet water. There a loud-voiced pond-larker spied him: and uttered such words as these. …

poems.title: Epigram I: To the Dwellers at Cyme
poems.excerpt: Have reverence for him who needs a home and stranger’s dole, all ye who dwell in the high city of Cyme, the lovely maiden, hard by the foothills of lofty Sardene, ye who drink the heavenly water of the divine stream, eddying Hermus, whom deathless Zeus begot.

poems.title: Epigram II
poems.excerpt: Speedily may my feet bear me to some town of righteous men; for their hearts are generous and their wit is best.

poems.title: Epigram III
poems.excerpt: I am a maiden of bronze and am set upon the tomb of Midas. While the waters flow and tall trees flourish, and the sun rises and shines and the bright moon also; while rivers run and the sea breaks on the shore, ever remaining on this mournful tomb, I tell the passer-by that Midas here lies buried.

poems.title: Epigram IV
poems.excerpt: To what a fate did Zeus the Father give me a prey even while he made me to grow, a babe at my mother’s knee! By the will of Zeus who holds the aegis the people of Phricon, riders on wanton horses, more active than raging fire in the test of war, once built the towers of Aeolian Smyrna, wave-shaken neighbour to the sea, through which glides the pleasant stream of sacred Meles; thence arose the daughters of Zeus, glorious children, and would fain have made famous that fair country and the city of its people. But in their folly those men scorned the divine voice and renown of song, and in trouble shall one of them remember this hereafter—he who with scornful words to them contrived my fate. Yet I will endure the lot which heaven gave me even at my birth, bearing my disappointment with a patient heart. My dear limbs yearn not to stay in the sacred streets of Cyme, but rather my great heart urges me to go unto another country, small though I am.

poems.title: Epigram V
poems.excerpt: Thestorides, full many things there are that mortals cannot sound; but there is nothing more unfathomable than the heart of man.

poems.title: Epigram VI
poems.excerpt: Hear me, Poseidon, strong shaker of the earth, ruler of wide-spread, tawny Helicon! Give a fair wind and sight of safe return to the shipmen who speed and govern this ship. And grant that when I come to the nether slopes of towering Mimas I may find honourable, god-fearing men. Also may I avenge me on the wretch who deceived me and grieved Zeus the lord of guests and his own guest-table.

poems.title: Epigram VII
poems.excerpt: Queen Earth, all bounteous giver of honey-hearted wealth, how kindly, it seems, you are to some, and how intractable and rough for those with whom you are angry.

poems.title: Epigram VIII
poems.excerpt: Sailors, who rove the seas and whom a hateful fate has made as the shy sea-fowl, living an unenviable life, observe the reverence due to Zeus who rules on high, the god of strangers; for terrible is the vengeance of this god afterwards for whosoever has sinned.

poems.title: Epigram IX
poems.excerpt: Strangers, a contrary wind has caught you: but even now take me aboard and you shall make your voyage.

poems.title: Epigram X
poems.excerpt: Another sort of pine shall bear a better fruit than you upon the heights of furrowed, windy Ida. For there shall mortal men get the iron that Ares loves so soon as the Cebrenians shall hold the land.

poems.title: Epigram XI
poems.excerpt: Glaucus, watchman of flocks, a word will I put in your heart. First give the dogs their dinner at the courtyard gate, for this is well. The dog first hears a man approaching and the wild-beast coming to the fence.

poems.title: Epigram XII
poems.excerpt: Goddess-nurse of the young, give ear to my prayer, and grant that this woman may reject the love-embraces of youth and dote on grey-haired old men whose powers are dulled, but whose hearts still desire.

poems.title: Epigram XIII
poems.excerpt: Children are a man’s crown, towers of a city; horses are the glory of a plain, and so are ships of the sea; wealth will make a house great, and reverend princes seated in assembly are a goodly sight for the folk to see. But a blazing fire makes a house look more comely upon a winter’s day, when the Son of Cronos sends down snow.

poems.title: Epigram XIV
poems.excerpt: Potters, if you will give me a reward, I will sing for you. Come, then, Athena, with hand upraised over the kiln. Let the pots and all the dishes turn out well and be well fired: let them fetch good prices and be sold in plenty in the market, and plenty in the streets. Grant that the potters may get great gain and grant me so to sing to them. But if you turn shameless and make false promises, then I call together the destroyers of kilns, Shatter and Smash and Charr and Crash and Crudebake who can work this craft much mischief. Come all of you and sack the kiln-yard and the buildings: let the whole kiln be shaken up to the potter’s loud lament. As a horse’s jaw grinds, so let the kiln grind to powder all the pots inside. And you, too, daughter of the Sun, Circe the witch, come and cast cruel spells; hurt both these men and their handiwork. Let Chiron also come and bring many Centaurs—all that escaped the hands of Heracles and all that were destroyed: let them make sad havoc of the pots and overthrow the kiln, and let the potters see the mischief and be grieved; but I will gloat as I behold their luckless craft. And if anyone of them stoops to peer in, let all his face be burned up, that all men may learn to deal honestly.

Open of yourselves, you doors, for mighty Wealth will enter in, and with Wealth comes jolly Mirth and gentle Peace. poems.title: Fragment 1
poems.excerpt: Immortal Aphrodite of the broidered throne, daughter of Zeus, weaver of wiles, I pray thee break not my spirit with anguish and distress, O Queen. But come hither, if ever before thou didst hear my voice afar, and listen, and leaving thy father's golden house camest with chariot yoked, and fair fleet sparrows drew thee, flapping fast their wings around the dark earth, from heaven through mid sky. Quickly arrived they; and thou, blessed one, smiling with immortal countenance, didst ask What now is befallen me, and Why now I call, and What I in my mad heart most desire to see. 'What Beauty now wouldst thou draw to love thee? Who wrongs thee, Sappho? For even if she flies she shall soon follow, and if she rejects gifts shall yet give, and if she loves not shall soon love, however loth.' Come, I pray thee, now too, and release me from cruel cares; and all that my heart desires to accomplish, accomplish thou, and be thyself my ally.

poems.title: Book VI, 218
poems.excerpt: A begging eunuch priest of Cybele was wandering through the upland forests of Ida, and there met him a huge lion, its hungry throat dreadfully gaping as though to devour him. Then in fear of the death that faced him in its ravening jaws, he beat his tambour from the holy grove. The lion shut its murderous mouth, and as if itself full of divine frenzy, began to toss and whirl its mane about its neck. But he thus escaping a dreadful death dedicated to Rhea the beast that had taught itself her dance.

poems.title: Book VII, 710
poems.excerpt: Ye columns and my Sirens, and thou, mournful pitcher that holdest the little ash of death, bid them who pass by my tomb hail, be they citizens or from another town; and tell this, too, that I was buried here a bride, and that my father called me Baucis, and that my country was Tenos, that they may know. Say, likewise, that my friend and companion Erinna engraved these lines on my tomb.

poems.title: Book VII, 712
poems.excerpt: I am the tomb of Baucis the bride, and as thou passest the much bewept pillar, say to Hades who dwells below “Hades, thou art envious.” To thee the fair letters thou seest on the stone will tell the most cruel fate of Bauco, how her bridegroom’s father lighted her pyre with those very torches that had burnt while they sang the marriage hymn. And thou, Hymenaeus, didst change the tuneful song of wedding to the dismal voice of lamentation.

poems.title: On a Betrothed Girl (Mackail)
poems.excerpt: I am of Baucis the bride; and passing by my oft-wept pillar thou mayest say this to Death that dwells under ground, "Thou art envious, O Death"; and the coloured monument tells to him who sees it the most bitter fortune of Bauco, how her father-in-law burned the girl on the funeral pyre with those torches by whose light the marriage train was to be led home; and thou, O Hymenaeus, didst change the tuneable bridal song into a voice of wailing dirges.

poems.title: Book VI, 134
poems.excerpt: Heliconias, she who holds the thyrsus, and Xanthippe next to her, and Glauce, are coming down the mountain on their way to the dance, and they are bringing for Dionysus ivy, grapes, and a fat goat.

poems.title: Book VI, 135
poems.excerpt: This horse of Phidolas from spacious Corinth is dedicated to Zeus in memory of the might of its legs.

poems.title: Book VI, 136
poems.excerpt: Praxipice worked and Dyseris designed this garment. It testifies to the skill of both.

poems.title: Book VI, 137
poems.excerpt: Apollo of the silver bow, grant willingly thy grace to Naucrates, the son of Aeschylus, receiving these his vows.

poems.title: Book VI, 138
poems.excerpt: Calliteles set me here of old, but this his descendants erected, to whom grant thy grace in return.

poems.title: Book VI, 139
poems.excerpt: Praxagoras, son of Lycaeus, dedicated these gifts to the gods. Anaxagoras was the craftsman.

poems.title: Book VI, 140
poems.excerpt: Metantuus, the son of Areiphilus, dedicated me to the wreath-loving son of Semele in memory of his victory in the dance.

poems.title: Book VI, 141
poems.excerpt: The shield that saved Python from the dread battle-din hangs in the precinct of Athene.

poems.title: Book VI, 142
poems.excerpt: Echecratidas, the ruler of Thessaly, dedicated me in honour of Bacchus and as a splendid ornament for his city.

poems.title: Book VI, 143: On a Statue of Hermes
poems.excerpt: Pray that the herald of the gods may be kind to Timonax, who placed me here to adorn this lovely porch, and as a gift to Hermes the Lord. In my gymnasium I receive whosoever wishes it, be he citizen or stranger.

poems.title: Book VI, 144
poems.excerpt: Leocrates, son of Stroebus, when thou didst dedicate this statue to Hermes, neither the beautiful-haired Graces were heedless of it, nor joyous Academe, in whose bosom I tell of thy beneficence to all who approach.

poems.title: Book VI, 145
poems.excerpt: Sophocles, who won the highest glory of the tragic Muse, first dedicated these altars to the gods.

poems.title: Book VI, 346
poems.excerpt: Give Tellis a pleasant life, O son of Maia, recompensing him for these sweet gifts; grant that he may dwell in the justly-ruled deme of Euonymea, enjoying good fortune all his days.

poems.title: Book VII, 160
poems.excerpt: Valiant in war was Timocritus, whose tomb this is. War is not sparing of the brave, but of cowards.

poems.title: Book VII, 226
poems.excerpt: This whole city acclaimed Agathon, the doughty warrior, as he lay on the pyre after dying for Abdera; for Ares greedy of blood slew no other young man like to him in the whirlwind of the dreadful fight.

poems.title: Book VII, 263
poems.excerpt: And thee too, Clenorides, homesickness drove to death when thou didst entrust thyself to the wintry blasts of the south wind. That faithless weather stayed thy journey and the wet seas washed out thy lovely youth.

poems.title: Book IX, 715
poems.excerpt: Herdsman, pasture thy herd far from here, lest taking Myron’s heifer to be alive thou drive it off with the rest.

poems.title: Book IX, 716
poems.excerpt: Myron pretended this heifer to be the work of his hands, but it was never formed in the mould, but turned into bronze owing to old age.

poems.title: Book XI, 47
poems.excerpt: I care not for the wealth of Gyges the King of Sardis, nor does gold take me captive, and I praise not tyrants. I care to drench my beard with scent and crown my head with roses. I care for to-day ; who knows to-morrow ?

poems.title: Book XI, 48
poems.excerpt: Moulding the silver make me, Hephaestus, no suit of armour, but fashion as deep as thou canst a hollow cup, and work on it neither stars nor chariots nor hateful Orion, but blooming vines and laughing clusters with lovely Bacchus.

poems.title: Book XIII, 4
poems.excerpt: I pity thee, Aristoclides, first among all my valiant friends. Thou didst lose thy young life, defending thy country from enslavement.

poems.title: On a Slain Warrior (Mackail)
poems.excerpt: Valiant in war was Timocritus, whose monument this is; but Ares spares the bad, not the good.
