The song that I came to sing remains unsung to this day.

I have spent my days in stringing and in unstringing my instrument. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 14: My desires are many and my cry
poems.excerpt:
My desires are many and my cry is pitiful, but ever didst thou save me by hard refusals; and this strong mercy has been wrought into my life through and through.

Day by day thou art making me worthy of the simple, great gifts that thou gavest to me unasked—this sky and the light, this body and the life and the mind—saving me from perils of overmuch desire. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 15: I am here to sing thee songs
poems.excerpt:
I am here to sing thee songs. In this hall of thine I have a corner seat.

In thy world I have no work to do; my useless life can only break out in tunes without a purpose. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 16: I have had my invitation to this world
poems.excerpt:
I have had my invitation to this world’s festival, and thus my life has been blessed. My eyes have seen and my ears have heard.

It was my part at this feast to play upon my instrument, and I have done all I could. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 17: I am only waiting for love to give
poems.excerpt:
I am only waiting for love to give myself up at last into his hands. That is why it is so late and why I have been guilty of such omissions.

They come with their laws and their codes to bind me fast; but I evade them ever, for I am only waiting for love to give myself up at last into his hands. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 18: Clouds heap upon clouds and it darkens
poems.excerpt:
Clouds heap upon clouds and it darkens. Ah, love, why dost thou let me wait outside at the door all alone?

In the busy moments of the noontide work I am with the crowd, but on this dark lonely day it is only for thee that I hope. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 19: If thou speakest not I will fill
poems.excerpt:
If thou speakest not I will fill my heart with thy silence and endure it. I will keep still and wait like the night with starry vigil and its head bent low with patience.

The morning will surely come, the darkness will vanish, and thy voice pour down in golden streams breaking through the sky. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 20: On the day when the lotus bloomed
poems.excerpt:
On the day when the lotus bloomed, alas, my mind was straying, and I knew it not. My basket was empty and the flower remained unheeded.

Only now and again a sadness fell upon me, and I started up from my dream and felt a sweet trace of a strange fragrance in the south wind. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 21: I must launch out my boat
poems.excerpt:
I must launch out my boat. The languid hours pass by on the shore—Alas for me!

The spring has done its flowering and taken leave. And now with the burden of faded futile flowers I wait and linger. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 22: In the deep shadows of the rainy July
poems.excerpt:
In the deep shadows of the rainy July, with secret steps, thou walkest, silent as night, eluding all watchers.

Today the morning has closed its eyes, heedless of the insistent calls of the loud east wind, and a thick veil has been drawn over the ever-wakeful blue sky. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 23: Art thou abroad on this stormy night
poems.excerpt:
Art thou abroad on this stormy night on thy journey of love, my friend? The sky groans like one in despair.

I have no sleep tonight. Ever and again I open my door and look out on the darkness, my friend! …

poems.title: Gitanjali 24: If the day is done
poems.excerpt:
If the day is done, if birds sing no more, if the wind has flagged tired, then draw the veil of darkness thick upon me, even as thou hast wrapt the earth with the coverlet of sleep and tenderly closed the petals of the drooping lotus at dusk.

From the traveller, whose sack of provisions is empty before the voyage is ended, whose garment is torn and dustladen, whose strength is exhausted, remove shame and poverty, and renew his life like a flower under the cover of thy kindly night.

poems.title: Gitanjali 25: In the night of weariness let me give
poems.excerpt:
In the night of weariness let me give myself up to sleep without struggle, resting my trust upon thee.

Let me not force my flagging spirit into a poor preparation for thy worship. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 26: He came and sat by my side
poems.excerpt:
He came and sat by my side but I woke not. What a cursed sleep it was, O miserable me!

He came when the night was still; he had his harp in his hands, and my dreams became resonant with its melodies. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 27: Light, oh where is the light
poems.excerpt:
Light, oh where is the light? Kindle it with the burning fire of desire!

There is the lamp but never a flicker of a flame—is such thy fate, my heart? Ah, death were better by far for thee! …

poems.title: Gitanjali 28: Obstinate are the trammels
poems.excerpt:
Obstinate are the trammels, but my heart aches when I try to break them.

Freedom is all I want, but to hope for it I feel ashamed. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 29: He whom I enclose with my name
poems.excerpt:
He whom I enclose with my name is weeping in this dungeon. I am ever busy building this wall all around; and as this wall goes up into the sky day by day I lose sight of my true being in its dark shadow.

I take pride in this great wall, and I plaster it with dust and sand lest a least hole should be left in this name; and for all the care I take I lose sight of my true being.

poems.title: Gitanjali 30: I came out alone on my way
poems.excerpt:
I came out alone on my way to my tryst. But who is this that follows me in the silent dark?

I move aside to avoid his presence but I escape him not. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 31: Prisoner, tell me
poems.excerpt:
“Prisoner, tell me, who was it that bound you?”

“It was my master,” said the prisoner. “I thought I could outdo everybody in the world in wealth and power, and I amassed in my own treasure-house the money due to my king. When sleep overcame me I lay upon the bed that was for my lord, and on waking up I found I was a prisoner in my own treasure-house.” …

poems.title: Gitanjali 32: By all means they try to hold
poems.excerpt:
By all means they try to hold me secure who love me in this world. But it is otherwise with thy love which is greater than theirs, and thou keepest me free.

Lest I forget them they never venture to leave me alone. But day passes by after day and thou art not seen. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 33: When it was day they came
poems.excerpt:
When it was day they came into my house and said, “We shall only take the smallest room here.”

They said, “We shall help you in the worship of your God and humbly accept only our own share in his grace”; and then they took their seat in a corner and they sat quiet and meek. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 34: Let only that little be left
poems.excerpt:
Let only that little be left of me whereby I may name thee my all.

Let only that little be left of my will whereby I may feel thee on every side, and come to thee in everything, and offer to thee my love every moment. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 35: Where the mind is without fear
poems.excerpt:
Where the mind is without fear and the head is held high;

Where knowledge is free; …

poems.title: Gitanjali 36: This is my prayer to thee
poems.excerpt:
This is my prayer to thee, my lord—strike, strike at the root of penury in my heart.

Give me the strength lightly to bear my joys and sorrows. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 37: I thought that my voyage had come
poems.excerpt:
I thought that my voyage had come to its end at the last limit of my power,—that the path before me was closed, that provisions were exhausted and the time come to take shelter in a silent obscurity.

But I find that thy will knows no end in me. And when old words die out on the tongue, new melodies break forth from the heart; and where the old tracks are lost, new country is revealed with its wonders.

poems.title: Gitanjali 38: That I want thee
poems.excerpt:
That I want thee, only thee—let my heart repeat without end. All desires that distract me, day and night, are false and empty to the core.

As the night keeps hidden in its gloom the petition for light, even thus in the depth of my unconsciousness rings the cry—I want thee, only thee. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 39: When the heart is hard and parched up
poems.excerpt:
When the heart is hard and parched up, come upon me with a shower of mercy.

When grace is lost from life, come with a burst of song. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 40: The rain has held back for days
poems.excerpt:
The rain has held back for days and days, my God, in my arid heart. The horizon is fiercely naked—not the thinnest cover of a soft cloud, not the vaguest hint of a distant cool shower.

Send thy angry storm, dark with death, if it is thy wish, and with lashes of lightning startle the sky from end to end. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 41: Where dost thou stand behind them all
poems.excerpt:
Where dost thou stand behind them all, my lover, hiding thyself in the shadows? They push thee and pass thee by on the dusty road, taking thee for naught. I wait here weary hours spreading my offerings for thee, while passers-by come and take my flowers, one by one, and my basket is nearly empty.

The morning time is past, and the noon. In the shade of evening my eyes are drowsy with sleep. Men going home glance at me and smile and fill me with shame. I sit like a beggar maid, drawing my skirt over my face, and when they ask me, what it is I want, I drop my eyes and answer them not. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 42: Early in the day it was whispered
poems.excerpt:
Early in the day it was whispered that we should sail in a boat, only thou and I, and never a soul in the world would know of this our pilgrimage to no country and to no end.

In that shoreless ocean, at thy silently listening smile my songs would swell in melodies, free as waves, free from all bondage of words. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 43: The day was when I did not keep
poems.excerpt:
The day was when I did not keep myself in readiness for thee; and entering my heart unbidden even as one of the common crowd, unknown to me, my king, thou didst press the signet of eternity upon many a fleeting moment of my life.

And today when by chance I light upon them and see thy signature, I find they have lain scattered in the dust mixed with the memory of joys and sorrows of my trivial days forgotten. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 44: This is my delight
poems.excerpt:
This is my delight, thus to wait and watch at the wayside where shadow chases light and the rain comes in the wake of the summer.

Messengers, with tidings from unknown skies, greet me and speed along the road. My heart is glad within, and the breath of the passing breeze is sweet. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 45: Have you not heard his silent steps
poems.excerpt:
Have you not heard his silent steps? He comes, comes, ever comes.

Every moment and every age, every day and every night he comes, comes, ever comes. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 46: I know not from what distant time
poems.excerpt:
I know not from what distant time thou art ever coming nearer to meet me. Thy sun and stars can never keep thee hidden from me for aye.

In many a morning and eve thy footsteps have been heard and thy messenger has come within my heart and called me in secret. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 47: The night is nearly spent waiting for him
poems.excerpt:
The night is nearly spent waiting for him in vain. I fear lest in the morning he suddenly come to my door when I have fallen asleep wearied out. Oh friends, leave the way open to him— forbid him not.

If the sounds of his steps does not wake me, do not try to rouse me, I pray. I wish not to be called from my sleep by the clamorous choir of birds, by the riot of wind at the festival of morning light. Let me sleep undisturbed even if my lord comes of a sudden to my door. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 48: The morning sea of silence broke into ripples
poems.excerpt:
The morning sea of silence broke into ripples of bird songs; and the flowers were all merry by the roadside; and the wealth of gold was scattered through the rift of the clouds while we busily went on our way and paid no heed.

We sang no glad songs nor played; we went not to the village for barter; we spoke not a word nor smiled; we lingered not on the way. We quickened our pace more and more as the time sped by. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 49: You came down from your throne and stood
poems.excerpt:
You came down from your throne and stood at my cottage door.

I was singing all alone in a corner, and the melody caught your ear. You came down and stood at my cottage door. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 50: I had gone a-begging from door to door
poems.excerpt:
I had gone a-begging from door to door in the village path, when thy golden chariot appeared in the distance like a gorgeous dream and I wondered who was this King of all kings!

My hopes rose high and methought my evil days were at an end, and I stood waiting for alms to be given unasked and for wealth scattered on all sides in the dust. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 51: The night darkened
poems.excerpt:
The night darkened. Our day’s works had been done. We thought that the last guest had arrived for the night and the doors in the village were all shut. Only some said the king was to come. We laughed and said “No, it cannot be!”

It seemed there were knocks at the door and we said it was nothing but the wind. We put out the lamps and lay down to sleep. Only some said, “It is the messenger!” We laughed and said “No, it must be the wind!” …

poems.title: Gitanjali 52: I thought I should ask of thee
poems.excerpt:
I thought I should ask of thee—but I dared not—the rose wreath thou hadst on thy neck. Thus I waited for the morning, when thou didst depart, to find a few fragments on the bed. And like a beggar I searched in the dawn only for a stray petal or two.

Ah me, what is it I find? What token left of thy love? It is no flower, no spices, no vase of perfumed water. It is thy mighty sword, flashing as a flame, heavy as a bolt of thunder. The young light of morning comes through the window and spreads itself upon thy bed. The morning bird twitters and asks, “Woman, what hast thou got?” No, it is no flower, nor spices, nor vase of perfumed water—it is thy dreadful sword. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 53: Beautiful is thy wristlet
poems.excerpt:
Beautiful is thy wristlet, decked with stars and cunningly wrought in myriad-coloured jewels. But more beautiful to me thy sword with its curve of lightning like the outspread wings of the divine bird of Vishnu, perfectly poised in the angry red light of the sunset.

It quivers like the one last response of life in ecstasy of pain at the final stroke of death; it shines like the pure flame of being burning up earthly sense with one fierce flash. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 54: I asked nothing from thee
poems.excerpt:
I asked nothing from thee; I uttered not my name to thine ear. When thou took’st thy leave I stood silent. I was alone by the well where the shadow of the tree fell aslant, and the women had gone home with their brown earthen pitchers full to the brim. They called me and shouted, “Come with us, the morning is wearing on to noon.” But I languidly lingered awhile lost in the midst of vague musings.

I heard not thy steps as thou camest. Thine eyes were sad when they fell on me; thy voice was tired as thou spokest low—“Ah, I am a thirsty traveller.” I started up from my day-dreams and poured water from my jar on thy joined palms. The leaves rustled overhead; the cuckoo sang from the unseen dark, and perfume of babla flowers came from the bend of the road. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 55: Languor is upon your heart and the slumber
poems.excerpt:
Languor is upon your heart and the slumber is still on your eyes.

Has not the word come to you that the flower is reigning in splendour among thorns? Wake, oh awaken! let not the time pass in vain! …

poems.title: Gitanjali 56: Thus it is that thy joy
poems.excerpt:
Thus it is that thy joy in me is so full. Thus it is that thou hast come down to me. O thou lord of all heavens, where would be thy love if I were not?

Thou hast taken me as thy partner of all this wealth. In my heart is the endless play of thy delight. In my life thy will is ever taking shape. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 57: Light, my light
poems.excerpt:
Light, my light, the world-filling light, the eye-kissing light, heart-sweetening light!

Ah, the light dances, my darling, at the centre of my life; the light strikes, my darling, the chords of my love; the sky opens, the wind runs wild, laughter passes over the earth. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 58: Let all the strains of joy mingle
poems.excerpt: Let all the strains of joy mingle in my last song—the joy that makes the earth flow over in the riotous excess of the grass, the joy that sets the twin brothers, life and death, dancing over the wide world, the joy that sweeps in with the tempest, shaking and waking all life with laughter, the joy that sits still with its tears on the open red lotus of pain, and the joy that throws everything it has upon the dust, and knows not a word.

poems.title: Gitanjali 59: Yes, I know
poems.excerpt:
Yes, I know, this is nothing but thy love, O beloved of my heart— this golden light that dances upon the leaves, these idle clouds sailing across the sky, this passing breeze leaving its coolness upon my forehead.

The morning light has flooded my eyes—this is thy message to my heart. Thy face is bent from above, thy eyes look down on my eyes, and my heart has touched thy feet.

poems.title: Gitanjali 60: On the seashore of endless worlds children meet
poems.excerpt:
On the seashore of endless worlds children meet. The infinite sky is motionless overhead and the restless water is boisterous. On the seashore of endless worlds the children meet with shouts and dances.

They build their houses with sand and they play with empty shells. With withered leaves they weave their boats and smilingly float them on the vast deep. Children have their play on the seashore of worlds. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 61: The sleep that flits on baby’s eyes
poems.excerpt:
The sleep that flits on baby’s eyes—does anybody know from where it comes? Yes, there is a rumour that it has its dwelling there, in the fairy village among shadows of the forest dimly lit with glow-worms, there hang two timid buds of enchantment. From there it comes to kiss baby’s eyes.

The smile that flickers on baby’s lips when he sleeps—does anybody know where it was born? Yes, there is a rumour that a young pale beam of a crescent moon touched the edge of a vanishing autumn cloud, and there the smile was first born in the dream of a dew-washed morning—the smile that flickers on baby’s lips when he sleeps. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 62: When I bring to you coloured toys
poems.excerpt:
When I bring to you coloured toys, my child, I understand why there is such a play of colours on clouds, on water, and why flowers are painted in tints—when I give coloured toys to you, my child.

When I sing to make you dance I truly now why there is music in leaves, and why waves send their chorus of voices to the heart of the listening earth—when I sing to make you dance. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 63: Thou hast made me known to friends
poems.excerpt:
Thou hast made me known to friends whom I knew not. Thou hast given me seats in homes not my own. Thou hast brought the distant near and made a brother of the stranger.

I am uneasy at heart when I have to leave my accustomed shelter; I forget that there abides the old in the new, and that there also thou abidest. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 64: On the slope of the desolate river
poems.excerpt:
On the slope of the desolate river among tall grasses I asked her, “Maiden, where do you go shading your lamp with your mantle? My house is all dark and lonesome—lend me your light!” she raised her dark eyes for a moment and looked at my face through the dusk. “I have come to the river,” she said, “to float my lamp on the stream when the daylight wanes in the west.” I stood alone among tall grasses and watched the timid flame of her lamp uselessly drifting in the tide.

In the silence of gathering night I asked her, “Maiden, your lights are all lit—then where do you go with your lamp? My house is all dark and lonesome—lend me your light.” She raised her dark eyes on my face and stood for a moment doubtful. “I have come,” she said at last, “to dedicate my lamp to the sky.” I stood and watched her light uselessly burning in the void. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 65: What divine drink wouldst thou have
poems.excerpt:
What divine drink wouldst thou have, my God, from this overflowing cup of my life?

My poet, is it thy delight to see thy creation through my eyes and to stand at the portals of my ears silently to listen to thine own eternal harmony? …

poems.title: Gitanjali 66: She who ever had remained in the depth
poems.excerpt:
She who ever had remained in the depth of my being, in the twilight of gleams and of glimpses; she who never opened her veils in the morning light, will be my last gift to thee, my God, folded in my final song.

Words have wooed yet failed to win her; persuasion has stretched to her its eager arms in vain. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 67: Thou art the sky and thou art
poems.excerpt:
Thou art the sky and thou art the nest as well.

O thou beautiful, there in the nest is thy love that encloses the soul with colours and sounds and odours. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 68: Thy sunbeam comes upon this earth of mine
poems.excerpt:
Thy sunbeam comes upon this earth of mine with arms outstretched and stands at my door the livelong day to carry back to thy feet clouds made of my tears and sighs and songs.

With fond delight thou wrappest about thy starry breast that mantle of misty cloud, turning it into numberless shapes and folds and colouring it with hues everchanging. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 69: The same stream of life that runs through
poems.excerpt:
The same stream of life that runs through my veins night and day runs through the world and dances in rhythmic measures.

It is the same life that shoots in joy through the dust of the earth in numberless blades of grass and breaks into tumultuous waves of leaves and flowers. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 70: Is it beyond thee to be glad
poems.excerpt:
Is it beyond thee to be glad with the gladness of this rhythm? to be tossed and lost and broken in the whirl of this fearful joy?

All things rush on, they stop not, they look not behind, no power can hold them back, they rush on. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 71: That I should make much of myself
poems.excerpt:
That I should make much of myself and turn it on all sides, thus casting coloured shadows on thy radiance—such is thy maya.

Thou settest a barrier in thine own being and then callest thy severed self in myriad notes. This thy self-separation has taken body in me. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 72: He it is
poems.excerpt:
He it is, the innermost one, who awakens my being with his deep hidden touches.

He it is who puts his enchantment upon these eyes and joyfully plays on the chords of my heart in varied cadence of pleasure and pain. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 73: Deliverance is not for me in renunciation
poems.excerpt:
Deliverance is not for me in renunciation. I feel the embrace of freedom in a thousand bonds of delight.

Thou ever pourest for me the fresh draught of thy wine of various colours and fragrance, filling this earthen vessel to the brim. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 74: The day is no more
poems.excerpt:
The day is no more, the shadow is upon the earth. It is time that I go to the stream to fill my pitcher.

The evening air is eager with the sad music of the water. Ah, it calls me out into the dusk. In the lonely lane there is no passer-by, the wind is up, the ripples are rampant in the river. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 75: Thy gifts to us mortals fulfil
poems.excerpt:
Thy gifts to us mortals fulfil all our needs and yet run back to thee undiminished.

The river has its everyday work to do and hastens through fields and hamlets; yet its incessant stream winds towards the washing of thy feet. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 76: Day after day
poems.excerpt:
Day after day, O lord of my life, shall I stand before thee face to face. With folded hands, O lord of all worlds, shall I stand before thee face to face.

Under thy great sky in solitude and silence, with humble heart shall I stand before thee face to face. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 77: I know thee as my God
poems.excerpt:
I know thee as my God and stand apart—I do not know thee as my own and come closer. I know thee as my father and bow before thy feet—I do not grasp thy hand as my friend’s.

I stand not where thou comest down and ownest thyself as mine, there to clasp thee to my heart and take thee as my comrade. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 78: When the creation was new
poems.excerpt:
When the creation was new and all the stars shone in their first splendour, the gods held their assembly in the sky and sang “Oh, the picture of perfection! the joy unalloyed!”

But one cried of a sudden—“It seems that somewhere there is a break in the chain of light and one of the stars has been lost.” …

poems.title: Gitanjali 79: If it is not my portion to meet
poems.excerpt:
If it is not my portion to meet thee in this life then let me ever feel that I have missed thy sight—let me not forget for a moment, let me carry the pangs of this sorrow in my dreams and in my wakeful hours.

As my days pass in the crowded market of this world and my hands grow full with the daily profits, let me ever feel that I have gained nothing—let me not forget for a moment, let me carry the pangs of this sorrow in my dreams and in my wakeful hours. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 80: I am like a remnant of a cloud
poems.excerpt:
I am like a remnant of a cloud of autumn uselessly roaming in the sky, O my sun ever-glorious! Thy touch has not yet melted my vapour, making me one with thy light, and thus I count months and years separated from thee.

If this be thy wish and if this be thy play, then take this fleeting emptiness of mine, paint it with colours, gild it with gold, float it on the wanton wind and spread it in varied wonders. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 81: On many an idle day have I grieved
poems.excerpt:
On many an idle day have I grieved over lost time. But it is never lost, my lord. Thou hast taken every moment of my life in thine own hands.

Hidden in the heart of things thou art nourishing seeds into sprouts, buds into blossoms, and ripening flowers into fruitfulness. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 82: Time is endless in thy hands
poems.excerpt:
Time is endless in thy hands, my lord. There is none to count thy minutes.

Days and nights pass and ages bloom and fade like flowers. Thou knowest how to wait. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 83: Mother, I shall weave a chain of pearls
poems.excerpt:
Mother, I shall weave a chain of pearls for thy neck with my tears of sorrow.

The stars have wrought their anklets of light to deck thy feet, but mine will hang upon thy breast. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 84: It is the pang of separation that spreads
poems.excerpt:
It is the pang of separation that spreads throughout the world and gives birth to shapes innumerable in the infinite sky.

It is this sorrow of separation that gazes in silence all nights from star to star and becomes lyric among rustling leaves in rainy darkness of July. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 85: When the warriors came out first
poems.excerpt:
When the warriors came out first from their master’s hall, where had they hid their power? Where were their armour and their arms?

They looked poor and helpless, and the arrows were showered upon them on the day they came out from their master’s hall. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 86: Death, thy servant
poems.excerpt:
Death, thy servant, is at my door. He has crossed the unknown sea and brought thy call to my home.

The night is dark and my heart is fearful—yet I will take up the lamp, open my gates and bow to him my welcome. It is thy messenger who stands at my door. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 87: In desperate hope I go and search
poems.excerpt:
In desperate hope I go and search for her in all the corners of my room; I find her not.

My house is small and what once has gone from it can never be regained. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 88: Deity of the ruined temple
poems.excerpt:
Deity of the ruined temple! The broken strings of Vina sing no more your praise. The bells in the evening proclaim not your time of worship. The air is still and silent about you.

In your desolate dwelling comes the vagrant spring breeze. It brings the tidings of flowers—the flowers that for your worship are offered no more. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 89: No more noisy
poems.excerpt:
No more noisy, loud words from me—such is my master’s will. Henceforth I deal in whispers. The speech of my heart will be carried on in murmurings of a song.

Men hasten to the King’s market. All the buyers and sellers are there. But I have my untimely leave in the middle of the day, in the thick of work. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 90: On the day when death will knock
poems.excerpt:
On the day when death will knock at thy door what wilt thou offer to him?

Oh, I will set before my guest the full vessel of my life—I will never let him go with empty hands. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 91: O thou the last fulfilment of life
poems.excerpt:
O thou the last fulfilment of life, Death, my death, come and whisper to me!

Day after day I have kept watch for thee; for thee have I borne the joys and pangs of life. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 92: I know that the day will come
poems.excerpt:
I know that the day will come when my sight of this earth shall be lost, and life will take its leave in silence, drawing the last curtain over my eyes.

Yet stars will watch at night, and morning rise as before, and hours heave like sea waves casting up pleasures and pains. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 93: I have got my leave
poems.excerpt:
I have got my leave. Bid me farewell, my brothers! I bow to you all and take my departure.

Here I give back the keys of my door—and I give up all claims to my house. I only ask for last kind words from you. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 94: At this time of my parting
poems.excerpt:
At this time of my parting, wish me good luck, my friends! The sky is flushed with the dawn and my path lies beautiful.

Ask not what I have with me to take there. I start on my journey with empty hands and expectant heart. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 95: I was not aware of the moment
poems.excerpt:
I was not aware of the moment when I first crossed the threshold of this life.

What was the power that made me open out into this vast mystery like a bud in the forest at midnight! …

poems.title: Gitanjali 96: When I go from hence
poems.excerpt:
When I go from hence let this be my parting word, that what I have seen is unsurpassable.

I have tasted of the hidden honey of this lotus that expands on the ocean of light, and thus am I blessed—let this be my parting word. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 97: When my play was with thee I never
poems.excerpt:
When my play was with thee I never questioned who thou wert. I knew nor shyness nor fear, my life was boisterous.

In the early morning thou wouldst call me from my sleep like my own comrade and lead me running from glade to glade. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 98: I will deck thee with trophies
poems.excerpt:
I will deck thee with trophies, garlands of my defeat. It is never in my power to escape unconquered.

I surely know my pride will go to the wall, my life will burst its bonds in exceeding pain, and my empty heart will sob out in music like a hollow reed, and the stone will melt in tears. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 99: When I give up the helm I know
poems.excerpt:
When I give up the helm I know that the time has come for thee to take it. What there is to do will be instantly done. Vain is this struggle.

Then take away your hands and silently put up with your defeat, my heart, and think it your good fortune to sit perfectly still where you are placed. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 100: I dive down into the depth
poems.excerpt:
I dive down into the depth of the ocean of forms, hoping to gain the perfect pearl of the formless.

No more sailing from harbour to harbour with this my weather-beaten boat. The days are long passed when my sport was to be tossed on waves. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 101: Ever in my life have I sought thee
poems.excerpt:
Ever in my life have I sought thee with my songs. It was they who led me from door to door, and with them have I felt about me, searching and touching my world.

It was my songs that taught me all the lessons I ever learnt; they showed me secret paths, they brought before my sight many a star on the horizon of my heart. …

poems.title: Gitanjali 102: I boasted among men that I had known
poems.excerpt:
I boasted among men that I had known you. They see your pictures in all works of mine. They come and ask me, “Who is he?” I know not how to answer them. I say, “Indeed, I cannot tell.” They blame me and they go away in scorn. And you sit there smiling.

I put my tales of you into lasting songs. The secret gushes out from my heart. They come and ask me, “Tell me all your meanings.” I know not how to answer them. I say, “Ah, who knows what they mean!” They smile and go away in utter scorn. And you sit there smiling.

poems.title: Gitanjali 103: In one salutation to thee
poems.excerpt:
In one salutation to thee, my God, let all my senses spread out and touch this world at thy feet.

Like a rain-cloud of July hung low with its burden of unshed showers let all my mind bend down at thy door in one salutation to thee. …

poems.title: The Gardener 1: Have mercy upon your servant
poems.excerpt:
SERVANT. Have mercy upon your servant, my queen!

QUEEN. The assembly is over and my servants are all gone. Why do you come at this late hour? …

poems.title: The Gardener 2: Ah, poet, the evening draws near
poems.excerpt:
"Ah, poet, the evening draws near; your hair is turning grey.
"Do you in your lonely musing hear the message of the hereafter?"
 …

poems.title: The Gardener 3: In the morning I cast my net
poems.excerpt:
In the morning I cast my net into the sea.
I dragged up from the dark abyss things of strange aspect and strange beauty--some shone like a smile, some glistened like tears, and some were flushed like the cheeks of a bride.
When with the day's burden I went home, my love was sitting in the garden idly tearing the leaves of a flower. …

poems.title: The Gardener 4: Ah me, why did they build my house
poems.excerpt:
Ah me, why did they build my house by the road to the market town?
They moor their laden boats near my trees.
They come and go and wander at their will. …

poems.title: The Gardener 5: I am restless
poems.excerpt:
I am restless. I am athirst for far-away things.
My soul goes out in a longing to touch the skirt of the dim distance.
O Great Beyond, O the keen call of thy flute! …

poems.title: The Gardener 6: The tame bird was in a cage
poems.excerpt:
The tame bird was in a cage, the free bird was in the forest.
They met when the time came, it was a decree of fate.
The free bird cries, "O my love, let us fly to wood." …

poems.title: The Gardener 7: O mother, the young Prince is to pass
poems.excerpt:
O mother, the young Prince is to pass by our door,--how can I attend to my work this morning?
Show me how to braid up my hair; tell me what garment to put on.
Why do you look at me amazed, mother? …

poems.title: The Gardener 8: When the lamp went out by my bed
poems.excerpt:
When the lamp went out by my bed I woke up with the early birds.
I sat at my open window with a fresh wreath on my loose hair.
The young traveller came along the road in the rosy mist of the morning. …

poems.title: The Gardener 9: When I go alone at night
poems.excerpt:
When I go alone at night to my love-tryst, birds do not sing, the wind does not stir, the houses on both sides of the street stand silent.
It is my own anklets that grow loud at every step and I am ashamed.
 …

poems.title: The Gardener 10: Let your work be
poems.excerpt:
Let your work be, bride. Listen, the guest has come.
Do you hear, he is gently shaking the chain which fastens the door?
See that your anklets make no loud noise, and that your step is not over-hurried at meeting him. …

poems.title: The Gardener 11: Come as you are
poems.excerpt:
Come as you are; do not loiter over your toilet.
If your braided hair has loosened, if the parting of your hair be not straight, if the ribbons of your bodice be not fastened, do not mind.
Come as you are; do not loiter over your toilet. …

poems.title: The Gardener 12: If you would be busy and fill
poems.excerpt:
If you would be busy and fill your pitcher, come, O come to my lake.
The water will cling round your feet and babble its secret.
The shadow of the coming rain is on the sands, and the clouds hang low upon the blue lines of the trees like the heavy hair above your eyebrows. …

poems.title: The Gardener 13: I asked nothing
poems.excerpt:
I asked nothing, only stood at the edge of the wood behind the tree.
Languor was still upon the eyes of the dawn, and the dew in the air.
The lazy smell of the damp grass hung in the thin mist above the earth. …

poems.title: The Gardener 14: I was walking by the road
poems.excerpt:
I was walking by the road, I do not know why, when the noonday was past and bamboo branches rustled in the wind.
The prone shadows with their out-stretched arms clung to the feet of the hurrying light.
The koels were weary of their songs. …

poems.title: The Gardener 15: I run as a musk-deer runs
poems.excerpt:
I run as a musk-deer runs in the shadow of the forest mad with his own perfume.
The night is the night of mid-May, the breeze is the breeze of the south.
I lose my way and I wander, I seek what I cannot get, I get what I do not seek. …

poems.title: The Gardener 16: Hands cling to hands and eyes linger
poems.excerpt:
Hands cling to hands and eyes linger on eyes: thus begins the record of our hearts.
It is the moonlit night of March; the sweet smell of henna is in the air; my flute lies on the earth neglected and your garland of flowers in unfinished.
This love between you and me is simple as a song. …

poems.title: The Gardener 17: The yellow bird sings in their tree
poems.excerpt:
The yellow bird sings in their tree and makes my heart dance with gladness.
We both live in the same village, and that is our one piece of joy.
Her pair of pet lambs come to graze in the shade of our garden trees. …

poems.title: The Gardener 18: When the two sisters go to fetch water
poems.excerpt:
When the two sisters go to fetch water, they come to this spot and they smile.
They must be aware of somebody who stands behind the trees whenever they go to fetch water.
 …

poems.title: The Gardener 19: You walked by the riverside path
poems.excerpt:
You walked by the riverside path with the full pitcher upon your hip.
Why did you swiftly turn your face and peep at me through your fluttering veil?
That gleaming look from the dark came upon me like a breeze that sends a shiver through the rippling water and sweeps away to the shadowy shore. …

poems.title: The Gardener 20: Day after day he comes and goes away
poems.excerpt:
Day after day he comes and goes away.
Go, and give him a flower from my hair, my friend.
If he asks who was it that sent it, I entreat you do not tell him my name--for he only comes and goes away. …

poems.title: The Gardener 21: Why did he choose to come
poems.excerpt:
Why did he choose to come to my door, the wandering youth, when the day dawned?
As I come in and out I pass by him every time, and my eyes are caught by his face.
I know not if I should speak to him or keep silent. Why did he choose to come to my door? …

poems.title: The Gardener 22: When she passed by me with quick steps
poems.excerpt:
When she passed by me with quick steps, the end of her skirt touched me.
From the unknown island of a heart came a sudden warm breath of spring.
A flutter of a flitting touch brushed me and vanished in a moment, like a torn flower petal blown in the breeze. …

poems.title: The Gardener 23: Why do you sit there and jingle
poems.excerpt:
Why do you sit there and jingle your bracelets in mere idle sport?
Fill your pitcher. It is time for you to come home.
 …

poems.title: The Gardener 24: Do not keep to yourself the secret
poems.excerpt:
Do not keep to yourself the secret of your heart, my friend!
Say it to me, only to me, in secret.
You who smile so gently, softly whisper, my heart will hear it, not my ears. …

poems.title: The Gardener 25: Come to us
poems.excerpt:
"Come to us, youth, tell us truly why there is madness in your eyes?"
"I know not what wine of wild poppy I have drunk, that there is this madness in my eyes."
"Ah, shame!" …

poems.title: The Gardener 26: What comes from your willing hands I take
poems.excerpt:
"What comes from your willing hands I take. I beg for nothing more."
"Yes, yes, I know you, modest mendicant, you ask for all that one has."
 …

poems.title: The Gardener 27: Trust love even if it brings sorrow
poems.excerpt:
"Trust love even if it brings sorrow. Do not close up your heart."
"Ah no, my friend, your words are dark, I cannot understand them."
 …

poems.title: The Gardener 28: Your questioning eyes are sad
poems.excerpt:
Your questioning eyes are sad. They seek to know my meaning as the moon would fathom the sea.
I have bared my life before your eyes from end to end, with nothing hidden or held back. That is why you know me not.
If it were only a gem I could break it into a hundred pieces and string them into a chain to put on your neck. …

poems.title: The Gardener 29: Speak to me
poems.excerpt:
Speak to me, my love! Tell me in words what you sang.
The night is dark. The stars are lost in clouds. The wind is sighing through the leaves.
I will let loose my hair. My blue cloak will cling round me like night. I will clasp your head to my bosom; and there in the sweet loneliness murmur on your heart. I will shut my eyes and listen. I will not look in your face. …

poems.title: The Gardener 30: You are the evening cloud floating
poems.excerpt:
You are the evening cloud floating in the sky of my dreams.
I paint you and fashion you ever with my love longings.
You are my own, my own, Dweller in my endless dreams! …

poems.title: The Gardener 31: My heart, the bird of the wilderness
poems.excerpt:
My heart, the bird of the wilderness, has found its sky in your eyes.
They are the cradle of the morning, they are the kingdom of the stars.
My songs are lost in their depths. …

poems.title: The Gardener 32: Tell me if this be all true
poems.excerpt:
Tell me if this be all true, my lover, tell me if this be true.
When these eyes flash their lightning the dark clouds in your breast make stormy answer.
Is it true that my lips are sweet like the opening bud of the first conscious love? …

poems.title: The Gardener 33: I love you
poems.excerpt:
I love you, beloved. Forgive me my love.
Like a bird losing its way I am caught.
When my heart was shaken it lost its veil and was naked. Cover it with pity, beloved, and forgive me my love. …

poems.title: The Gardener 34: Do not go
poems.excerpt:
Do not go, my love, without asking my leave.
I have watched all night, and now my eyes are heavy with sleep.
I fear lest I lose you when I am sleeping. …

poems.title: The Gardener 35: Lest I should know you too easily
poems.excerpt:
Lest I should know you too easily, you play with me.
You blind me with flashes of laughter to hide your tears.
I know, I know your art. …

poems.title: The Gardener 36: He whispered, My love
poems.excerpt:
He whispered, "My love, raise your eyes."
I sharply chid him, and said "Go!"; but he did not stir.
He stood before me and held both my hands. I said, "Leave me!"; but he did not go. …

poems.title: The Gardener 37: Would you put your wreath of fresh flowers
poems.excerpt:
Would you put your wreath of fresh flowers on my neck, fair one?
But you must know that the one wreath that I had woven is for the many, for those who are seen in glimpses, or dwell in lands unexplored, or live in poets' songs.
 …

poems.title: The Gardener 38: My love, once upon a time your poet
poems.excerpt:
My love, once upon a time your poet launched a great epic in his mind.
Alas, I was not careful, and it struck your ringing anklets and came to grief.
It broke up into scraps of songs and lay scattered at your feet. …

poems.title: The Gardener 39: I try to weave a wreath
poems.excerpt:
I try to weave a wreath all the morning, but the flowers slip and they drop out.
You sit there watching me in secret through the corner of your prying eyes.
Ask those eyes, darkly planning mischief, whose fault it was. …

poems.title: The Gardener 40: An unbelieving smile flits on your eyes
poems.excerpt:
An unbelieving smile flits on your eyes when I come to you to take my leave.
I have done it so often that you think I will soon return.
To tell you the truth I have the same doubt in my mind. …

poems.title: The Gardener 41: I long to speak the deepest words
poems.excerpt:
I long to speak the deepest words I have to say to you; but I dare not, for fear you should laugh.
That is why I laugh at myself and shatter my secret in jest.
I make light of my pain, afraid you should do so. …

poems.title: The Gardener 42: O mad, superbly drunk
The Gardener 43: No, my friends
poems.excerpt:
No, my friends, I shall never be an ascetic, whatever you may say.
I shall never be an ascetic if she does not take the vow with me.
It is my firm resolve that if I cannot find a shady shelter and a companion for my penance, I shall never turn ascetic. …

poems.title: The Gardener 44: Reverend sir, forgive this pair of sinners
poems.excerpt:
Reverend sir, forgive this pair of sinners. Spring winds to-day are blowing in wild eddies, driving dust and dead leaves away, and with them your lessons are all lost.
Do not say, father, that life is a vanity.
For we have made truce with death for once, and only for a few fragrant hours we two have been made immortal. …

poems.title: The Gardener 45: To the guests that must go
poems.excerpt:
To the guests that must go bid God's speed and brush away all traces of their steps.
Take to your bosom with a smile what is easy and simple and near.
To-day is the festival of phantoms that know not when they die. …

poems.title: The Gardener 46: You left me and went on your way
poems.excerpt:
You left me and went on your way.
I thought I should mourn for you and set your solitary image in my heart wrought in a golden song.
But ah, my evil fortune, time is short. …

poems.title: The Gardener 47: If you would have it so
poems.excerpt:
If you would have it so, I will end my singing.
If it sets your heart aflutter, I will take away my eyes from your face.
If it suddenly startles you in your walk, I will step aside and take another path. …

poems.title: The Gardener 48: Free me from the bonds of your sweetness
poems.excerpt:
Free me from the bonds of your sweetness, my love! No more of this wine of kisses.
This mist of heavy incense stifles my heart.
Open the doors, make room for the morning light. …

poems.title: The Gardener 49: I hold her hands and press
poems.excerpt:
I hold her hands and press her to my breast.
I try to fill my arms with her loveliness, to plunder her sweet smile with kisses, to drink her dark glances with my eyes.
Ah, but, where is it? Who can strain the blue from the sky? …

poems.title: The Gardener 50: Love, my heart longs day and night
poems.excerpt:
Love, my heart longs day and night for the meeting with you--for the meeting that is like all-devouring death.
Sweep me away like a storm; take everything I have; break open my sleep and plunder my dreams. Rob me of my world.
In that devastation, in the utter nakedness of spirit, let us become one in beauty. …

poems.title: The Gardener 51: Then finish the last song and let us
poems.excerpt:
Then finish the last song and let us leave.
Forget this night when the night is no more.
Whom do I try to clasp in my arms? Dreams can never be made captive. …

poems.title: The Gardener 52: Why did the lamp go out
poems.excerpt:
Why did the lamp go out?
I shaded it with my cloak to save it from the wind, that is why the lamp went out.
 …

poems.title: The Gardener 53: Why do you put me to shame
poems.excerpt:
Why do you put me to shame with a look?
I have not come as a beggar.
Only for a passing hour I stood at the end of your courtyard outside the garden hedge. …

poems.title: The Gardener 54: Where do you hurry with your basket
poems.excerpt:
Where do you hurry with your basket this late evening when the marketing is over?
They all have come home with their burdens; the moon peeps from above the village trees.
The echoes of the voices calling for the ferry run across the dark water to the distant swamp where wild ducks sleep. …

poems.title: The Gardener 55: It was mid-day when you went away
poems.excerpt:
It was mid-day when you went away.
The sun was strong in the sky.
I had done my work and sat alone on my balcony when you went away. …

poems.title: The Gardener 56: I was one among many women busy
poems.excerpt:
I was one among many women busy with the obscure daily tasks of the household.
Why did you single me out and bring me away from the cool shelter of our common life?
 …

poems.title: The Gardener 57: I plucked your flower
poems.excerpt:
I plucked your flower, O world!
I pressed it to my heart and the thorn pricked.
When the day waned and it darkened, I found that the flower had faded, but the pain remained. …

poems.title: The Gardener 58: One morning in the flower garden a blind
poems.excerpt:
One morning in the flower garden a blind girl came to offer me a flower chain in the cover of a lotus leaf.
I put it round my neck, and tears came to my eyes.
I kissed her and said, "You are blind even as the flowers are. …

poems.title: The Gardener 59: O woman, you are not merely the handiwork
poems.excerpt:
O woman, you are not merely the handiwork of God, but also of men; these are ever endowing you with beauty from their hearts.
Poets are weaving for you a web with threads of golden imagery; painters are giving your form ever new immortality.
The sea gives its pearls, the mines their gold, the summer gardens their flowers to deck you, to cover you, to make you more precious. …

poems.title: The Gardener 60: Amidst the rush and roar of life
poems.excerpt:
Amidst the rush and roar of life, O Beauty, carved in stone, you stand mute and still, alone and aloof.
Great Time sits enamoured at your feet and murmurs:
"Speak, speak to me, my love; speak, my bride!" …

poems.title: The Gardener 61: Peace, my heart
poems.excerpt:
Peace, my heart, let the time for the parting be sweet.
Let it not be a death but completeness.
Let love melt into memory and pain into songs. …

poems.title: The Gardener 62: In the dusky path of a dream
poems.excerpt:
In the dusky path of a dream I went to seek the love who was mine in a former life.

Her house stood at the end of a desolate street. …

poems.title: The Gardener 63: Traveller, must you go
poems.excerpt:
Traveller, must you go?
The night is still and the darkness swoons upon the forest.
The lamps are bright in our balcony, the flowers all fresh, and the youthful eyes still awake. …

poems.title: The Gardener 64: I spent my day on the scorching hot
poems.excerpt:
I spent my day on the scorching hot dust of the road.
Now, in the cool of the evening, I knock at the door of the inn. It is deserted and in ruins.
A grim ashath tree spreads its hungry clutching roots through the gaping fissures of the walls. …

poems.title: The Gardener 65: Is that your call again
poems.excerpt:
Is that your call again?
The evening has come. Weariness clings around me like the arms of entreating love.
Do you call me? …

poems.title: The Gardener 66: A wandering madman was seeking the touchstone
poems.excerpt:
A wandering madman was seeking the touchstone, with matted locks tawny and dust-laden, and body worn to a shadow, his lips tight-pressed, like the shut-up doors of his heart, his burning eyes like the lamp of a glow-worm seeking its mate.

Before him the endless ocean roared. …

poems.title: The Gardener 67: Though the evening comes with slow steps
The Gardener 68: None lives for ever
poems.excerpt:
None lives for ever, brother, and nothing lasts for long. Keep that in mind and rejoice.
Our life is not the one old burden, our path is not the one long journey.
One sole poet has not to sing one aged song. …

poems.title: The Gardener 69: I hunt for the golden stag
poems.excerpt:
I hunt for the golden stag.
You may smile, my friends, but I pursue the vision that eludes me.
I run across hills and dales, I wander through nameless lands, because I am hunting for the golden stag. …

poems.title: The Gardener 70: I remember a day in my childhood
poems.excerpt:
I remember a day in my childhood I floated a paper boat in the ditch.
It was a wet day of July; I was alone and happy over my play.
I floated my paper boat in the ditch. …

poems.title: The Gardener 71: The day is not yet done
poems.excerpt:
The day is not yet done, the fair is not over, the fair on the river-bank.
I had feared that my time had been squandered and my last penny lost.
But no, my brother, I have still something left. My fate has not cheated me of everything. …

poems.title: The Gardener 72: With days of hard travail I raised
poems.excerpt:
With days of hard travail I raised a temple. It had no doors or windows, its walls were thickly built with massive stones.
I forgot all else, I shunned all the world, I gazed in rapt contemplation at the image I had set upon the altar.
It was always night inside, and lit by the lamps of perfumed oil. …

poems.title: The Gardener 73: Infinite wealth is not yours
poems.excerpt:
Infinite wealth is not yours, my patient and dusky mother dust!
You toil to fill the mouths of your children, but food is scarce.
The gift of gladness that you have for us is never perfect. …

poems.title: The Gardener 74: In the world's audience hall
poems.excerpt:
In the world's audience hall, the simple blade of grass sits on the same carpet with the sunbeam and the stars of midnight.
Thus my songs share their seats in the heart of the world with the music of the clouds and forests.
But, you man of riches, your wealth has no part in the simple grandeur of the sun's glad gold and the mellow gleam of the musing moon. …

poems.title: The Gardener 75: At midnight the would-be ascetic announced
poems.excerpt:
At midnight the would-be ascetic announced:
"This is the time to give up my home and seek for God. Ah, who has held me so long in delusion here?"
God whispered, "I," but the ears of the man were stopped. …

poems.title: The Gardener 76: The fair was on before the temple
poems.excerpt:
The fair was on before the temple. It had rained from the early morning and the day came to its end.
Brighter than all the gladness of the crowd was the bright smile of a girl who bought for a farthing a whistle of palm leaf.
The shrill joy of that whistle floated above all laughter and noise. …

poems.title: The Gardener 77: The workman and his wife from the west
poems.excerpt:
The workman and his wife from the west country are busy digging to make bricks for the kiln.
Their little daughter goes to the landing-place by the river; there she has no end of scouring and scrubbing of pots and pans.
Her little brother, with shaven head and brown, naked, mud- covered limbs, follows after her and waits patiently on the high bank at her bidding. …

poems.title: The Gardener 78: It was in May
poems.excerpt:
It was in May. The sultry noon seemed endlessly long. The dry earth gaped with thirst in the heat.
When I heard from the riverside a voice calling, "Come, my darling!"
I shut my book and opened the window to look out. …

poems.title: The Gardener 79: I often wonder where lie hidden the boundaries
poems.excerpt:
I often wonder where lie hidden the boundaries of recognition between man and the beast whose heart knows no spoken language.
Through what primal paradise in a remote morning of creation ran the simple path by which their hearts visited each other.
Those marks of their constant tread have not been effaced though their kinship has been long forgotten. …

poems.title: The Gardener 80: With a glance of your eyes you could
poems.excerpt:
With a glance of your eyes you could plunder all the wealth of songs struck from poets' harps, fair woman!
But for their praises you have no ear, therefore I come to praise you.
You could humble at your feet the proudest heads in the world. …

poems.title: The Gardener 81: Why do you whisper so faintly
poems.excerpt:
Why do you whisper so faintly in my ears, O Death, my Death?
When the flowers droop in the evening and cattle come back to their stalls, you stealthily come to my side and speak words that I do not understand.
Is this how you must woo and win me with the opiate of drowsy murmur and cold kisses, O Death, my Death? …

poems.title: The Gardener 82: We are to play the game of death
poems.excerpt:
We are to play the game of death to-night, my bride and I.
The night is black, the clouds in the sky are capricious, and the waves are raving at sea.
We have left our bed of dreams, flung open the door and come out, my bride and I. …

poems.title: The Gardener 83: She dwelt on the hillside by the edge
poems.excerpt:
She dwelt on the hillside by the edge of a maize-field, near the spring that flows in laughing rills through the solemn shadows of ancient trees. The women came there to fill their jars, and travellers would sit there to rest and talk. She worked and dreamed daily to the tune of the bubbling stream.

One evening the stranger came down from the cloud-hidden peak; his locks were tangled like drowsy snakes. We asked in wonder, "Who are you?" He answered not but sat by the garrulous stream and silently gazed at the hut where she dwelt. Our hearts quaked in fear and we came back home when it was night. …

poems.title: The Gardener 84: Over the green and yellow rice-fields sweep
poems.excerpt:
Over the green and yellow rice-fields sweep the shadows of the autumn clouds followed by the swift chasing sun.
The bees forget to sip their honey; drunken with light they foolishly hover and hum.
The ducks in the islands of the river clamour in joy for mere nothing. …

poems.title: The Gardener 85: Who are you
poems.excerpt:
Who are you, reader, reading my poems an hundred years hence?
I cannot send you one single flower from this wealth of the spring, one single streak of gold from yonder clouds.
Open your doors and look abroad. …

poems.title: Stray Birds 1: Stray birds of summer come to my window
poems.excerpt:
Stray birds of summer come to my window to sing and fly away.
And yellow leaves of autumn, which have no songs, flutter and fall there with a sigh.

poems.title: Stray Birds 2: O troupe of little vagrants of the world
poems.excerpt: O troupe of little vagrants of the world, leave your footprints in my words.

poems.title: Stray Birds 3: The world puts off its mask of vastness
poems.excerpt:
The world puts off its mask of vastness to its lover.
It becomes small as one song, as one kiss of the eternal.

poems.title: Stray Birds 4: It is the tears of the earth that
poems.excerpt: It is the tears of the earth that keep her smiles in bloom.

poems.title: Stray Birds 5: The mighty desert is burning for the love
poems.excerpt: The mighty desert is burning for the love of a blade of grass who shakes her head and laughs and flies away.

poems.title: Stray Birds 6: If you shed tears when you miss the
poems.excerpt: If you shed tears when you miss the sun, you also miss the stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 7: The sands in your way beg for your
poems.excerpt: The sands in your way beg for your song and your movement, dancing water.  Will you carry the burden of their lameness?

poems.title: Stray Birds 8: Her wistful face haunts my dreams like the
poems.excerpt: Her wistful face haunts my dreams like the rain at night.

poems.title: Stray Birds 9: Once we dreamt that we were strangers
poems.excerpt:
Once we dreamt that we were strangers.
We wake up to find that we were dear to each other.

poems.title: Stray Birds 10: Sorrow is hushed into peace in my heart
poems.excerpt: Sorrow is hushed into peace in my heart like the evening among the silent trees.

poems.title: Stray Birds 11: Some unseen fingers
poems.excerpt: Some unseen fingers, like idle breeze, are playing upon my heart the music of the ripples.

poems.title: Stray Birds 12: "What language is thine
poems.excerpt:
"What language is thine, O sea?"

"The language of eternal question." …

poems.title: Stray Birds 13: Listen
poems.excerpt: Listen, my heart, to the whispers of the world with which it makes love to you.

poems.title: Stray Birds 14: The mystery of creation is like the darkness
poems.excerpt: The mystery of creation is like the darkness of night—it is great.  Delusions of knowledge are like the fog of the morning.

poems.title: Stray Birds 15: Do not seat your love upon a precipice
poems.excerpt: Do not seat your love upon a precipice because it is high.

poems.title: Stray Birds 16: I sit at my window this morning where
poems.excerpt: I sit at my window this morning where the world like a passer-by stops for a moment, nods to me and goes.

poems.title: Stray Birds 17: These little thoughts are the rustle of leaves
poems.excerpt: These little thoughts are the rustle of leaves; they have their whisper of joy in my mind.

poems.title: Stray Birds 18: What you are you do not see
poems.excerpt: What you are you do not see, what you see is your shadow.

poems.title: Stray Birds 19: My wishes are fools
poems.excerpt:
My wishes are fools, they shout across thy songs, my Master.
Let me but listen.

poems.title: Stray Birds 20: I cannot choose the best
poems.excerpt:
I cannot choose the best.
The best chooses me.

poems.title: Stray Birds 21: They throw their shadows before them who carry
poems.excerpt: They throw their shadows before them who carry their lantern on their back.

poems.title: Stray Birds 22: That I exist is a perpetual surprise which
poems.excerpt: That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life.

poems.title: Stray Birds 23: "We
poems.excerpt:
"We, the rustling leaves, have a voice that answers the storms, but who are you so silent?"

"I am a mere flower."

poems.title: Stray Birds 24: Rest belongs to the work as the eyelids
poems.excerpt: Rest belongs to the work as the eyelids to the eyes.

poems.title: Stray Birds 25: Man is a born child
poems.excerpt: Man is a born child, his power is the power of growth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 26: God expects answers for the flowers he sends
poems.excerpt: God expects answers for the flowers he sends us, not for the sun and the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 27: The light that plays
poems.excerpt: The light that plays, like a naked child, among the green leaves happily knows not that man can lie.

poems.title: Stray Birds 28: O Beauty
poems.excerpt: O Beauty, find thyself in love, not in the flattery of thy mirror.

poems.title: Stray Birds 29: My heart beats her waves at the shore
poems.excerpt: My heart beats her waves at the shore of the world and writes upon it her signature in tears with the words, "I love thee."

poems.title: Stray Birds 30: "Moon
poems.excerpt:
"Moon, for what do you wait?"

"To salute the sun for whom I must make way."

poems.title: Stray Birds 31: The trees come up to my window like
poems.excerpt: The trees come up to my window like the yearning voice of the dumb earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 32: His own mornings are new surprises to God
poems.excerpt: His own mornings are new surprises to God.

poems.title: Stray Birds 33: Life finds its wealth by the claims of
poems.excerpt: Life finds its wealth by the claims of the world, and its worth by the claims of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 34: The dry river-bed finds no thanks for its
poems.excerpt: The dry river-bed finds no thanks for its past.

poems.title: Stray Birds 35: The bird wishes it were a cloud
poems.excerpt: The bird wishes it were a cloud.  The cloud wishes it were a bird.

poems.title: Stray Birds 36: The waterfall sings
poems.excerpt: The waterfall sings, "I find my song, when I find my freedom."

poems.title: Stray Birds 37: I cannot tell why this heart languishes in
poems.excerpt:
I cannot tell why this heart languishes in silence.
It is for small needs it never asks, or knows or remembers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 38: Woman
poems.excerpt: Woman, when you move about in your household service your limbs sing like a hill stream among its pebbles.

poems.title: Stray Birds 39: The sun goes to cross the Western sea
poems.excerpt: The sun goes to cross the Western sea, leaving its last salutation to the East.

poems.title: Stray Birds 40: Do not blame your food because you have
poems.excerpt: Do not blame your food because you have no appetite.

poems.title: Stray Birds 41: The trees
poems.excerpt: The trees, like the longings of the earth, stand a-tiptoe to peep at the heaven.

poems.title: Stray Birds 42: You smiled and talked to me of nothing
poems.excerpt: You smiled and talked to me of nothing and I felt that for this I had been waiting long.

poems.title: Stray Birds 43: The fish in the water is silent
poems.excerpt: The fish in the water is silent, the animal on the earth is noisy, the bird in the air is singing, But Man has in him the silence of the sea, the noise of the earth and the music of the air.

poems.title: Stray Birds 44: The world rushes on over the strings of
poems.excerpt: The world rushes on over the strings of the lingering heart making the music of sadness.

poems.title: Stray Birds 45: He has made his weapons his gods
poems.excerpt: He has made his weapons his gods.  When his weapons win he is defeated himself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 46: God finds himself by creating
poems.excerpt: God finds himself by creating.

poems.title: Stray Birds 47: Shadow
poems.excerpt: Shadow, with her veil drawn, follows Light in secret meekness, with her silent steps of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 48: The stars are not afraid to appear like
poems.excerpt: The stars are not afraid to appear like fireflies.

poems.title: Stray Birds 49: I thank thee that I am none of
poems.excerpt: I thank thee that I am none of the wheels of power but I am one with the living creatures that are crushed by it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 50: The mind
poems.excerpt: The mind, sharp but not broad, sticks at every point but does not move.

poems.title: Stray Birds 51: Your idol is shattered in the dust to
poems.excerpt: Your idol is shattered in the dust to prove that God's dust is greater than your idol.

poems.title: Stray Birds 52: Man does not reveal himself in his history
poems.excerpt: Man does not reveal himself in his history, he struggles up through it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 53: While the glass lamp rebukes the earthen for
poems.excerpt: While the glass lamp rebukes the earthen for calling it cousin, the moon rises, and the glass lamp, with a bland smile, calls her, "My dear, dear sister."

poems.title: Stray Birds 54: Like the meeting of the seagulls and the
poems.excerpt: Like the meeting of the seagulls and the waves we meet and come near.  The seagulls fly off, the waves roll away and we depart.

poems.title: Stray Birds 55: My day is done
poems.excerpt: My day is done, and I am like a boat drawn on the beach, listening to the dance-music of the tide in the evening.

poems.title: Stray Birds 56: Life is given to us
poems.excerpt: Life is given to us, we earn it by giving it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 57: We come nearest to the great when we
poems.excerpt: We come nearest to the great when we are great in humility.

poems.title: Stray Birds 58: The sparrow is sorry for the peacock at
poems.excerpt: The sparrow is sorry for the peacock at the burden of its tail.

poems.title: Stray Birds 59: Never be afraid of the moments
poems.excerpt: Never be afraid of the moments—thus sings the voice of the everlasting.

poems.title: Stray Birds 60: The hurricane seeks the shortest road by the
poems.excerpt: The hurricane seeks the shortest road by the no-road, and suddenly ends its search in the Nowhere.

poems.title: Stray Birds 61: Take my wine in my own cup
poems.excerpt:
Take my wine in my own cup, friend.
It loses its wreath of foam when poured into that of others.

poems.title: Stray Birds 62: The Perfect decks itself in beauty for the
poems.excerpt: The Perfect decks itself in beauty for the love of the Imperfect.

poems.title: Stray Birds 63: God says to man
poems.excerpt: God says to man, "I heal you therefore I hurt, love you therefore punish."

poems.title: Stray Birds 64: Thank the flame for its light
poems.excerpt: Thank the flame for its light, but do not forget the lampholder standing in the shade with constancy of patience.

poems.title: Stray Birds 65: Tiny grass
poems.excerpt: Tiny grass, your steps are small, but you possess the earth under your tread.

poems.title: Stray Birds 66: The infant flower opens its bud and cries
poems.excerpt: The infant flower opens its bud and cries, "Dear World, please do not fade."

poems.title: Stray Birds 67: God grows weary of great kingdoms
poems.excerpt: God grows weary of great kingdoms, but never of little flowers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 68: Wrong cannot afford defeat but Right can
poems.excerpt: Wrong cannot afford defeat but Right can.

poems.title: Stray Birds 69: "I give my whole water in joy," sings
poems.excerpt: "I give my whole water in joy," sings the waterfall, "though little of it is enough for the thirsty."

poems.title: Stray Birds 70: Where is the fountain that throws up these
poems.excerpt: Where is the fountain that throws up these flowers in a ceaseless outbreak of ecstasy?

poems.title: Stray Birds 71: The woodcutter's axe begged for its handle from
poems.excerpt:
The woodcutter's axe begged for its handle from the tree.
The tree gave it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 72: In my solitude of heart I feel the
poems.excerpt: In my solitude of heart I feel the sigh of this widowed evening veiled with mist and rain.

poems.title: Stray Birds 73: Chastity is a wealth that comes from abundance
poems.excerpt: Chastity is a wealth that comes from abundance of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 74: The mist
poems.excerpt: The mist, like love, plays upon the heart of the hills and brings out surprises of beauty.

poems.title: Stray Birds 75: We read the world wrong and say that
poems.excerpt: We read the world wrong and say that it deceives us.

poems.title: Stray Birds 76: The poet wind is out over the sea
poems.excerpt: The poet wind is out over the sea and the forest to seek his own voice.

poems.title: Stray Birds 77: Every child comes with the message that God
poems.excerpt: Every child comes with the message that God is not yet discouraged of man.

poems.title: Stray Birds 78: The grass seeks her crowd in the earth
poems.excerpt:
The grass seeks her crowd in the earth.
The tree seeks his solitude of the sky.

poems.title: Stray Birds 79: Man barricades against himself
poems.excerpt: Man barricades against himself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 80: Your voice
poems.excerpt: Your voice, my friend, wanders in my heart, like the muffled sound of the sea among these listening pines.

poems.title: Stray Birds 81: What is this unseen flame of darkness whose
poems.excerpt: What is this unseen flame of darkness whose sparks are the stars?

poems.title: Stray Birds 82: Let life be beautiful like summer flowers and
poems.excerpt: Let life be beautiful like summer flowers and death like autumn leaves.

poems.title: Stray Birds 83: He who wants to do good knocks at
poems.excerpt: He who wants to do good knocks at the gate; he who loves finds the gate open.

poems.title: Stray Birds 84: In death the many becomes one
poems.excerpt:
In death the many becomes one; in life the one becomes many.
Religion will be one when God is dead.

poems.title: Stray Birds 85: The artist is the lover of Nature
poems.excerpt: The artist is the lover of Nature, therefore he is her slave and her master.

poems.title: Stray Birds 86: "How far are you from me
poems.excerpt:
"How far are you from me, O Fruit?"

"I am hidden in your heart, O Flower."

poems.title: Stray Birds 87: This longing is for the one who is
poems.excerpt: This longing is for the one who is felt in the dark, but not seen in the day.

poems.title: Stray Birds 88: "You are the big drop of dew under
poems.excerpt: "You are the big drop of dew under the lotus leaf, I am the smaller one on its upper side," said the dewdrop to the lake.

poems.title: Stray Birds 89: The scabbard is content to be dull when
poems.excerpt: The scabbard is content to be dull when it protects the keenness of the sword.

poems.title: Stray Birds 90: In darkness the One appears as uniform
poems.excerpt: In darkness the One appears as uniform; in the light the One appears as manifold.

poems.title: Stray Birds 91: The great earth makes herself hospitable with the
poems.excerpt: The great earth makes herself hospitable with the help of the grass.

poems.title: Stray Birds 92: The birth and death of the leaves are
poems.excerpt: The birth and death of the leaves are the rapid whirls of the eddy whose wider circles move slowly among stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 93: Power said to the world
poems.excerpt:
Power said to the world, "You are mine.

The world kept it prisoner on her throne. …

poems.title: Stray Birds 94: The mist is like the earth's desire
poems.excerpt: The mist is like the earth's desire.  It hides the sun for whom she cries.

poems.title: Stray Birds 95: Be still
poems.excerpt: Be still, my heart, these great trees are prayers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 96: The noise of the moment scoffs at the
poems.excerpt: The noise of the moment scoffs at the music of the Eternal.

poems.title: Stray Birds 97: I think of other ages that floated upon
poems.excerpt: I think of other ages that floated upon the stream of life and love and death and are forgotten, and I feel the freedom of passing away.

poems.title: Stray Birds 98: The sadness of my soul is her bride's
poems.excerpt:
The sadness of my soul is her bride's veil.
It waits to be lifted in the night.

poems.title: Stray Birds 99: Death's stamp gives value to the coin of
poems.excerpt: Death's stamp gives value to the coin of life; making it possible to buy with life what is truly precious.

poems.title: Stray Birds 100: The cloud stood humbly in a corner of
poems.excerpt:
The cloud stood humbly in a corner of the sky.
The morning crowned it with splendour.

poems.title: Stray Birds 101: The dust receives insult and in return offers
poems.excerpt: The dust receives insult and in return offers her flowers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 102: Do not linger to gather flowers to keep
poems.excerpt: Do not linger to gather flowers to keep them, but walk on, for flowers will keep themselves blooming all your way.

poems.title: Stray Birds 103: Roots are the branches down in the earth
poems.excerpt:
Roots are the branches down in the earth.
Branches are roots in the air.

poems.title: Stray Birds 104: The music of the far-away summer flutters around
poems.excerpt: The music of the far-away summer flutters around the Autumn seeking its former nest.

poems.title: Stray Birds 105: Do not insult your friend by lending him
poems.excerpt: Do not insult your friend by lending him merits from your own pocket.

poems.title: Stray Birds 106: The touch of the nameless days clings to
poems.excerpt: The touch of the nameless days clings to my heart like mosses round the old tree.

poems.title: Stray Birds 107: The echo mocks her origin to prove she
poems.excerpt: The echo mocks her origin to prove she is the original.

poems.title: Stray Birds 108: God is ashamed when the prosperous boasts of
poems.excerpt: God is ashamed when the prosperous boasts of His special favour.

poems.title: Stray Birds 109: I cast my own shadow upon my path
poems.excerpt: I cast my own shadow upon my path, because I have a lamp that has not been lighted.

poems.title: Stray Birds 110: Man goes into the noisy crowd to drown
poems.excerpt: Man goes into the noisy crowd to drown his own clamour of silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 111: That which ends in exhaustion is death
poems.excerpt: That which ends in exhaustion is death, but the perfect ending is in the endless.

poems.title: Stray Birds 112: The sun has his simple robe of light
poems.excerpt: The sun has his simple robe of light.  The clouds are decked with gorgeousness.

poems.title: Stray Birds 113: The hills are like shouts of children who
poems.excerpt: The hills are like shouts of children who raise their arms, trying to catch stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 114: The road is lonely in its crowd for
poems.excerpt: The road is lonely in its crowd for it is not loved.

poems.title: Stray Birds 115: The power that boasts of its mischiefs is
poems.excerpt: The power that boasts of its mischiefs is laughed at by the yellow leaves that fall, and clouds that pass by.

poems.title: Stray Birds 116: The earth hums to me to-day in the
poems.excerpt: The earth hums to me to-day in the sun, like a woman at her spinng, some ballad of the ancient time in a forgotten tongue.

poems.title: Stray Birds 117: The grass-blade is worth of the great world
poems.excerpt: The grass-blade is worth of the great world where it grows.

poems.title: Stray Birds 118: Dream is a wife who must talk
poems.excerpt:
Dream is a wife who must talk.
Sleep is a husband who silently suffers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 119: The night kisses the fading day whispering to
poems.excerpt: The night kisses the fading day whispering to his ear, "I am death, your mother.  I am to give you fresh birth."

poems.title: Stray Birds 120: I feel
poems.excerpt: I feel, thy beauty, dark night, like that of the loved woman when she has put out the lamp.

poems.title: Stray Birds 121: I carry in my world that flourishes the
poems.excerpt: I carry in my world that flourishes the worlds that have failed.

poems.title: Stray Birds 122: Dear friend
poems.excerpt: Dear friend, I feel the silence of your great thoughts of may a deepening eventide on this beach when I listen to these waves.

poems.title: Stray Birds 123: The bird thinks it is an act of
poems.excerpt: The bird thinks it is an act of kindness to give the fish a lift in the air.

poems.title: Stray Birds 124: "In the moon thou sendest thy love letters
poems.excerpt:
"In the moon thou sendest thy love letters to me," said the night to the sun.

"I leave my answers in tears upon the grass."

poems.title: Stray Birds 125: The Great is a born child
poems.excerpt: The Great is a born child; when he dies he gives his great childhood to the world.

poems.title: Stray Birds 126: Not hammerstrokes
poems.excerpt: Not hammerstrokes, but dance of the water sings the pebbles into perfection.

poems.title: Stray Birds 127: Bees sip honey from flowers and hum their
poems.excerpt:
Bees sip honey from flowers and hum their thanks when they leave.
The gaudy butterfly is sure that the flowers owe thanks to him.

poems.title: Stray Birds 128: To be outspoken is easy when you do
poems.excerpt: To be outspoken is easy when you do not wait to speak the complete truth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 129: Asks the Possible to the Impossible
poems.excerpt:
Asks the Possible to the Impossible, "Where is your dwelling place?"

"In the dreams of the impotent," comes the answer.

poems.title: Stray Birds 130: If you shut your door to all errors
