poems.excerpt: If you shut your door to all errors truth will be shut out.

poems.title: Stray Birds 131: I hear some rustle of things behind my
poems.excerpt: I hear some rustle of things behind my sadness of heart,—I cannot see them.

poems.title: Stray Birds 132: Leisure in its activity is work
poems.excerpt:
Leisure in its activity is work.
The stillness of the sea stirs in waves.

poems.title: Stray Birds 133: The leaf becomes flower when it loves
poems.excerpt:
The leaf becomes flower when it loves.
The flower becomes fruit when it worships.

poems.title: Stray Birds 134: The roots below the earth claim no rewards
poems.excerpt: The roots below the earth claim no rewards for making the branches fruitful.

poems.title: Stray Birds 135: This rainy evening the wind is restless
poems.excerpt:
This rainy evening the wind is restless.
I look at the swaying branches and ponder over the greatness of all things.

poems.title: Stray Birds 136: Storm of midnight
poems.excerpt: Storm of midnight, like a giant child awakened in the untimely dark, has begun to play and shout.

poems.title: Stray Birds 137: Thou raisest thy waves vainly to follow thy
poems.excerpt: Thou raisest thy waves vainly to follow thy lover.  O sea, thou lonely bride of the storm.

poems.title: Stray Birds 138: "I am ashamed of my emptiness," said the
poems.excerpt:
"I am ashamed of my emptiness," said the Word to the Work.
"I know how poor I am when I see you," said the Work to the Word.

poems.title: Stray Birds 139: Time is the wealth of change
poems.excerpt: Time is the wealth of change, but the clock in its parody makes it mere change and no wealth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 140: Truth in her dress finds facts too tight
poems.excerpt:
Truth in her dress finds facts too tight.
In fiction she moves with ease.

poems.title: Stray Birds 141: When I travelled to here and to there
poems.excerpt: When I travelled to here and to there, I was tired of thee, O Road, but now when thou leadest me to everywhere I am wedded to thee in love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 142: Let me think that there is one among
poems.excerpt: Let me think that there is one among those stars that guides my life through the dark unknown.

poems.title: Stray Birds 143: Woman
poems.excerpt: Woman, with the grace of your fingers you touched my things and order came out like music.

poems.title: Stray Birds 144: One sad voice has its nest among the
poems.excerpt:
One sad voice has its nest among the ruins of the years.
It sings to me in the night,—"I loved you."

poems.title: Stray Birds 145: The flaming fire warns me off by its
poems.excerpt:
The flaming fire warns me off by its own glow.
Save me from the dying embers hidden under ashes.

poems.title: Stray Birds 146: I have my stars in the sky
poems.excerpt: I have my stars in the sky, But oh for my little lamp unlit in my house.

poems.title: Stray Birds 147: The dust of the dead words clings to
poems.excerpt:
The dust of the dead words clings to thee.
Wash thy soul with silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 148: Gaps are left in life through which comes
poems.excerpt: Gaps are left in life through which comes the sad music of death.

poems.title: Stray Birds 149: The world has opened its heart of light
poems.excerpt:
The world has opened its heart of light in the morning.
Come out, my heart, with thy love to meet it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 150: My thoughts shimmer with these shimmering leaves and
poems.excerpt: My thoughts shimmer with these shimmering leaves and my heart sings with the touch of this sunlight; my life is glad to be floating with all things into the blue of space, into the dark of time.

poems.title: Stray Birds 151: God's great power is in the gentle breeze
poems.excerpt: God's great power is in the gentle breeze, not in the storm.

poems.title: Stray Birds 152: This is a dream in which things are
poems.excerpt:
This is a dream in which things are all loose and they oppress.
I shall find them gathered in thee when I awake and shall be free.

poems.title: Stray Birds 153: "Who is there to take up my duties?"
poems.excerpt:
"Who is there to take up my duties?"  asked the setting sun.

"I shall do what I can, my Master," said the earthen lamp.

poems.title: Stray Birds 154: By plucking her petals you do not gather
poems.excerpt: By plucking her petals you do not gather the beauty of the flower.

poems.title: Stray Birds 155: Silence will carry your voice like the nest
poems.excerpt: Silence will carry your voice like the nest that holds the sleeping birds.

poems.title: Stray Birds 156: The Great walks with the Small without fear
poems.excerpt:
The Great walks with the Small without fear.
The Middling keeps aloof.

poems.title: Stray Birds 157: The night opens the flowers in secret and
poems.excerpt: The night opens the flowers in secret and allows the day to get thanks.

poems.title: Stray Birds 158: Power takes as ingratitude the writhings of its
poems.excerpt: Power takes as ingratitude the writhings of its victims.

poems.title: Stray Birds 159: When we rejoice in our fulness
poems.excerpt: When we rejoice in our fulness, then we can part with our fruits with joy.

poems.title: Stray Birds 160: The raindrops kissed the earth and whispered
poems.excerpt: The raindrops kissed the earth and whispered,—"We are thy homesick children, mother, come back to thee from the heaven."

poems.title: Stray Birds 161: The cobweb pretends to catch dew-drops and catches
poems.excerpt: The cobweb pretends to catch dew-drops and catches flies.

poems.title: Stray Birds 162: Love
poems.excerpt: Love!  when you come with the burning lamp of pain in your hand, I can see your face and know you as bliss.

poems.title: Stray Birds 163: "The learned say that your lights will one
poems.excerpt:
"The learned say that your lights will one day be no more."  said the firefly to the stars.

The stars made no answer.

poems.title: Stray Birds 164: In the dusk of the evening the bird
poems.excerpt: In the dusk of the evening the bird of some early dawn comes to the nest of my silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 165: Thoughts pass in my mind like flocks of
poems.excerpt:
Thoughts pass in my mind like flocks of ducks in the sky.
I hear the voice of their wings.

poems.title: Stray Birds 166: The canal loves to think that rivers exist
poems.excerpt: The canal loves to think that rivers exist solely to supply it with water.

poems.title: Stray Birds 167: The world has kissed my soul with its
poems.excerpt: The world has kissed my soul with its pain, asking for its return in songs.

poems.title: Stray Birds 168: That which oppresses me
poems.excerpt: That which oppresses me, is it my soul trying to come out in the open, or the soul of the world knocking at my heart for its entrance?

poems.title: Stray Birds 169: Thought feeds itself with its own words and
poems.excerpt: Thought feeds itself with its own words and grows.

poems.title: Stray Birds 170: I have dipped the vessel of my heart
poems.excerpt: I have dipped the vessel of my heart into this silent hour; it has filled with love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 171: Either you have work or you have not
poems.excerpt:
Either you have work or you have not.
When you have to say, "Let us do something," then begins mischief.

poems.title: Stray Birds 172: The sunflower blushed to own the nameless flower
poems.excerpt:
The sunflower blushed to own the nameless flower as her kin.
The sun rose and smiled on it, saying, "Are you well, my darling?"

poems.title: Stray Birds 173: "Who drives me forward like fate?" "The Myself
poems.excerpt:
"Who drives me forward like fate?"

"The Myself striding on my back."

poems.title: Stray Birds 174: The clouds fill the watercups of the river
poems.excerpt: The clouds fill the watercups of the river, hiding themselves in the distant hills.

poems.title: Stray Birds 175: I spill water from my water jar as
poems.excerpt: I spill water from my water jar as I walk on my way, Very little remains for my home.

poems.title: Stray Birds 176: The water in a vessel is sparkling
poems.excerpt:
The water in a vessel is sparkling; the water in the sea is dark.
The small truth has words that are clear; the great truth has great silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 177: Your smile was the flowers of your own
poems.excerpt: Your smile was the flowers of your own fields, your talk was the rustle of your own mountain pines, but your heart was the woman that we all know.

poems.title: Stray Birds 178: It is the little things that I leave
poems.excerpt: It is the little things that I leave behind for my loved ones,— great things are for everyone.

poems.title: Stray Birds 179: Woman
poems.excerpt: Woman, thou hast encircled the world's heart with the depth of thy tears as the sea has the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 180: The sunshine greets me with a smile
poems.excerpt: The sunshine greets me with a smile.  The rain, his sad sister, talks to my heart.

poems.title: Stray Birds 181: My flower of the day dropped its petals
poems.excerpt:
My flower of the day dropped its petals forgotten.
In the evening it ripens into a golden fruit of memory.

poems.title: Stray Birds 182: I am like the road in the night
poems.excerpt: I am like the road in the night listening to the footfalls of its memories in silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 183: The evening sky to me is like a
poems.excerpt: The evening sky to me is like a window, and a lighted lamp, and a waiting behind it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 184: He who is too busy doing good finds
poems.excerpt: He who is too busy doing good finds no time to be good.

poems.title: Stray Birds 185: I am the autumn cloud
poems.excerpt: I am the autumn cloud, empty of rain, see my fulness in the field of ripened rice.

poems.title: Stray Birds 186: They hated and killed and men praised them
poems.excerpt:
They hated and killed and men praised them.
But God in shame hastens to hide its memory under the green grass.

poems.title: Stray Birds 187: Toes are the fingers that have forsaken their
poems.excerpt: Toes are the fingers that have forsaken their past.

poems.title: Stray Birds 188: Darkness travels towards light
poems.excerpt: Darkness travels towards light, but blindness towards death.

poems.title: Stray Birds 189: The pet dog suspects the universe for scheming
poems.excerpt: The pet dog suspects the universe for scheming to take its place.

poems.title: Stray Birds 190: Sit still my heart
poems.excerpt:
Sit still my heart, do not raise your dust.
Let the world find its way to you.

poems.title: Stray Birds 191: The bow whispers to the arrow before it
poems.excerpt: The bow whispers to the arrow before it speeds forth—"Your freedom is mine."

poems.title: Stray Birds 192: Woman
poems.excerpt: Woman, in your laughter you have the music of the fountain of life.

poems.title: Stray Birds 193: A mind all logic is like a knife
poems.excerpt:
A mind all logic is like a knife all blade.
It makes the hand bleed that uses it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 194: God loves man's lamp lights better than his
poems.excerpt: God loves man's lamp lights better than his own great stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 195: This world is the world of wild storms
poems.excerpt: This world is the world of wild storms kept tame with the music of beauty.

poems.title: Stray Birds 196: "My heart is like the golden casket of
poems.excerpt: "My heart is like the golden casket of thy kiss," said the sunset cloud to the sun.

poems.title: Stray Birds 197: By touching you may kill
poems.excerpt: By touching you may kill, by keeping away you may possess.

poems.title: Stray Birds 198: The cricket's chirp and the patter of rain
poems.excerpt: The cricket's chirp and the patter of rain come to me through the dark, like the rustle of dreams from my past youth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 199: "I have lost my dewdrop," cries the flower
poems.excerpt: "I have lost my dewdrop," cries the flower to the morning sky that has lost all its stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 200: The burning log bursts in flame and cries
poems.excerpt: The burning log bursts in flame and cries,—"This is my flower, my death."

poems.title: Stray Birds 201: The wasp thinks that the honey-hive of the
poems.excerpt:
The wasp thinks that the honey-hive of the neighbouring bees is too small.
His neighbours ask him to build one still smaller.

poems.title: Stray Birds 202: "I cannot keep your waves," says the bank
poems.excerpt:
"I cannot keep your waves," says the bank to the river.

"Let me keep your footprints in my heart."

poems.title: Stray Birds 203: The day
poems.excerpt: The day, with the noise of this little earth, drowns the silence of all worlds.

poems.title: Stray Birds 204: The song feels the infinite in the air
poems.excerpt: The song feels the infinite in the air, the picture in the earth, the poem in the air and the earth; For its words have meaning that walks and music that soars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 205: When the sun goes down to the West
poems.excerpt: When the sun goes down to the West, the East of his morning stands before him in silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 206: Let me not put myself wrongly to my
poems.excerpt: Let me not put myself wrongly to my world and set it against me.

poems.title: Stray Birds 207: Praise shames me
poems.excerpt: Praise shames me, for I secretly beg for it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 208: Let my doing nothing when I have nothing
poems.excerpt: Let my doing nothing when I have nothing to do become untroubled in its depth of peace like the evening in the seashore when the water is silent.

poems.title: Stray Birds 209: Maiden
poems.excerpt: Maiden, your simplicity, like the blueness of the lake, reveals your depth of truth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 210: The best does not come alone
poems.excerpt: The best does not come alone.  It comes with the company of the all.

poems.title: Stray Birds 211: God's right hand is gentle
poems.excerpt: God's right hand is gentle, but terrible is his left hand.

poems.title: Stray Birds 212: My evening came among the alien trees and
poems.excerpt: My evening came among the alien trees and spoke in a language which my morning stars did not know.

poems.title: Stray Birds 213: Night's darkness is a bag that bursts with
poems.excerpt: Night's darkness is a bag that bursts with the gold of the dawn.

poems.title: Stray Birds 214: Our desire lends the colours of the rainbow
poems.excerpt: Our desire lends the colours of the rainbow to the mere mists and vapours of life.

poems.title: Stray Birds 215: God waits to win back his own flowers
poems.excerpt: God waits to win back his own flowers as gifts from man's hands.

poems.title: Stray Birds 216: My sad thoughts tease me asking me their
poems.excerpt: My sad thoughts tease me asking me their own names.

poems.title: Stray Birds 217: The service of the fruit is precious
poems.excerpt: The service of the fruit is precious, the service of the flower is sweet, but let my service be the service of the leaves in its shade of humble devotion.

poems.title: Stray Birds 218: My heart has spread its sails to the
poems.excerpt: My heart has spread its sails to the idle winds for the shadowy island of Anywhere.

poems.title: Stray Birds 219: Men are cruel
poems.excerpt: Men are cruel, but Man is kind.

poems.title: Stray Birds 220: Make me thy cup and let my fulness
poems.excerpt: Make me thy cup and let my fulness be for thee and for thine.

poems.title: Stray Birds 221: The storm is like the cry of some
poems.excerpt: The storm is like the cry of some god in pain whose love the earth refuses.

poems.title: Stray Birds 222: The world does not leak because death is
poems.excerpt: The world does not leak because death is not a crack.

poems.title: Stray Birds 223: Life has become richer by the love that
poems.excerpt: Life has become richer by the love that has been lost.

poems.title: Stray Birds 224: My friend
poems.excerpt: My friend, your great heart shone with the sunrise of the East like the snowy summit of a lonely hill in the dawn.

poems.title: Stray Birds 225: The fountain of death makes the still water
poems.excerpt: The fountain of death makes the still water of life play.

poems.title: Stray Birds 226: Those who have everything but thee
poems.excerpt: Those who have everything but thee, my God, laugh at those who have nothing but thyself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 227: The movement of life has its rest in
poems.excerpt: The movement of life has its rest in its own music.

poems.title: Stray Birds 228: Kicks only raise dust and not crops from
poems.excerpt: Kicks only raise dust and not crops from the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 229: Our names are the light that glows on
poems.excerpt: Our names are the light that glows on the sea waves at night and then dies without leaving its signature.

poems.title: Stray Birds 230: Let him only see the thorns who has
poems.excerpt: Let him only see the thorns who has eyes to see the rose.

poems.title: Stray Birds 231: Set bird's wings with gold and it will
poems.excerpt: Set bird's wings with gold and it will never again soar in the sky.

poems.title: Stray Birds 232: The same lotus of our clime blooms here
poems.excerpt: The same lotus of our clime blooms here in the alien water with the same sweetness, under another name.

poems.title: Stray Birds 233: In heart's perspective the distance looms large
poems.excerpt: In heart's perspective the distance looms large.

poems.title: Stray Birds 234: The moon has her light all over the
poems.excerpt: The moon has her light all over the sky, her dark spots to herself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 235: Do not say
poems.excerpt: Do not say, "It is morning," and dismiss it with a name of yesterday.  See it for the first time as a new-born child that has no name.

poems.title: Stray Birds 236: Smoke boasts to the sky
poems.excerpt: Smoke boasts to the sky, and Ashes to the earth, that they are brothers to the fire.

poems.title: Stray Birds 237: The raindrop whispered to the jasmine
poems.excerpt:
The raindrop whispered to the jasmine, "Keep me in your heart for ever."

The jasmine sighed, "Alas," and dropped to the ground.

poems.title: Stray Birds 238: Timid thoughts
poems.excerpt:
Timid thoughts, do not be afraid of me.
I am a poet.

poems.title: Stray Birds 239: The dim silence of my mind seems filled
poems.excerpt: The dim silence of my mind seems filled with crickets' chirp—the grey twilight of sound.

poems.title: Stray Birds 240: Rockets
poems.excerpt: Rockets, your insult to the stars follows yourself back to the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 241: Thou hast led me through my crowded travels
poems.excerpt:
Thou hast led me through my crowded travels of the day to my evening's loneliness.
I wait for its meaning through the stillness of the night.

poems.title: Stray Birds 242: This life is the crossing of a sea
poems.excerpt:
This life is the crossing of a sea, where we meet in the same narrow ship.
In death we reach the shore and go to our different worlds.

poems.title: Stray Birds 243: The stream of truth flows through its channels
poems.excerpt: The stream of truth flows through its channels of mistakes.

poems.title: Stray Birds 244: My heart is homesick to-day for the one
poems.excerpt: My heart is homesick to-day for the one sweet hour across the sea of time.

poems.title: Stray Birds 245: The bird-song is the echo of the morning
poems.excerpt: The bird-song is the echo of the morning light back from the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 246: "Are you too proud to kiss me?" the
poems.excerpt: "Are you too proud to kiss me?"  the morning light asks the buttercup.

poems.title: Stray Birds 247: "How may I sing to thee and worship
poems.excerpt:
"How may I sing to thee and worship, O Sun?"  asked the little flower.

"By the simple silence of thy purity," answered the sun.

poems.title: Stray Birds 248: Man is worse than an animal when he
poems.excerpt: Man is worse than an animal when he is an animal.

poems.title: Stray Birds 249: Dark clouds become heaven's flowers when kissed by
poems.excerpt: Dark clouds become heaven's flowers when kissed by light.

poems.title: Stray Birds 250: Let not the sword-blade mock its handle for
poems.excerpt: Let not the sword-blade mock its handle for being blunt.

poems.title: Stray Birds 251: The night's silence
poems.excerpt: The night's silence, like a deep lamp, is burning with the light of its milky way.

poems.title: Stray Birds 252: Around the sunny island of Life swells day
poems.excerpt: Around the sunny island of Life swells day and night death's limitless song of the sea.

poems.title: Stray Birds 253: Is not this mountain like a flower
poems.excerpt: Is not this mountain like a flower, with its petals of hills, drinking the sunlight?

poems.title: Stray Birds 254: The real with its meaning read wrong and
poems.excerpt: The real with its meaning read wrong and emphasis misplaced is the unreal.

poems.title: Stray Birds 255: Find your beauty
poems.excerpt: Find your beauty, my heart, from the world's movement, like the boat that has the grace of the wind and the water.

poems.title: Stray Birds 256: The eyes are not proud of their sight
poems.excerpt: The eyes are not proud of their sight but of their eyeglasses.

poems.title: Stray Birds 257: I live in this little world of mine
poems.excerpt: I live in this little world of mine and am afraid to make it the least less.  Lift me into thy world and let me have the freedom gladly to lose my all.

poems.title: Stray Birds 258: The false can never grow into truth by
poems.excerpt: The false can never grow into truth by growing in power.

poems.title: Stray Birds 259: My heart
poems.excerpt: My heart, with its lapping waves of song, longs to caress this green world of the sunny day.

poems.title: Stray Birds 260: Wayside grass
poems.excerpt: Wayside grass, love the star, then your dreams will come out in flowers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 261: Let your music
poems.excerpt: Let your music, like a sword, pierce the noise of the market to its heart.

poems.title: Stray Birds 262: The trembling leaves of this tree touch my
poems.excerpt: The trembling leaves of this tree touch my heart like the fingers of an infant child.

poems.title: Stray Birds 263: This sadness of my soul is her bride's
poems.excerpt:
This sadness of my soul is her bride's veil.
It waits to be lifted in the night.

poems.title: Stray Birds 264: The little flower lies in the dust
poems.excerpt:
The little flower lies in the dust.
It sought the path of the butterfly.

poems.title: Stray Birds 265: I am in the world of the roads
poems.excerpt: I am in the world of the roads.  The night comes.  Open thy gate, thou world of the home.

poems.title: Stray Birds 266: I have sung the songs of thy day
poems.excerpt: I have sung the songs of thy day.  In the evening let me carry thy lamp through the stormy path.

poems.title: Stray Birds 267: I do not ask thee into the house
poems.excerpt:
I do not ask thee into the house.
Come into my infinite loneliness, my Lover.

poems.title: Stray Birds 268: Death belongs to life as birth does
poems.excerpt: Death belongs to life as birth does.  The walk is in the raising of the foot as in the laying of it down.

poems.title: Stray Birds 269: I have learnt the simple meaning of thy
poems.excerpt: I have learnt the simple meaning of thy whispers in flowers and sunshine—teach me to know thy words in pain and death.

poems.title: Stray Birds 270: The night's flower was late when the morning
poems.excerpt: The night's flower was late when the morning kissed her, she shivered and sighed and dropped to the ground.

poems.title: Stray Birds 271: Through the sadness of all things I hear
poems.excerpt: Through the sadness of all things I hear the crooning of the Eternal Mother.

poems.title: Stray Birds 272: I came to your shore as a stranger
poems.excerpt: I came to your shore as a stranger, I lived in your house as a guest, I leave your door as a friend, my earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 273: Let my thoughts come to you
poems.excerpt: Let my thoughts come to you, when I am gone, like the afterglow of sunset at the margin of starry silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 274: Light in my heart the evening star of
poems.excerpt: Light in my heart the evening star of rest and then let the night whisper to me of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 275: I am a child in the dark
poems.excerpt:
I am a child in the dark.
I stretch my hands through the coverlet of night for thee, Mother.

poems.title: Stray Birds 276: The day of work is done
poems.excerpt:
The day of work is done.  Hide my face in your arms, Mother.
Let me dream.

poems.title: Stray Birds 277: The lamp of meeting burns long
poems.excerpt: The lamp of meeting burns long; it goes out in a moment at the parting.

poems.title: Stray Birds 278: One word keep for me in thy silence
poems.excerpt: One word keep for me in thy silence, O World, when I am dead, "I have loved."

poems.title: Stray Birds 279: We live in this world when we love
poems.excerpt: We live in this world when we love it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 280: Let the dead have the immortality of fame
poems.excerpt: Let the dead have the immortality of fame, but the living the immortality of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 281: I have seen thee as the half-awakened child
poems.excerpt: I have seen thee as the half-awakened child sees his mother in the dusk of the dawn and then smiles and sleeps again.

poems.title: Stray Birds 282: I shall die again and again to know
poems.excerpt: I shall die again and again to know that life is inexhaustible.

poems.title: Stray Birds 283: While I was passing with the crowd in
poems.excerpt: While I was passing with the crowd in the road I saw thy smile from the balcony and I sang and forgot all noise.

poems.title: Stray Birds 284: Love is life in its fulness like the
poems.excerpt: Love is life in its fulness like the cup with its wine.

poems.title: Stray Birds 285: They light their own lamps and sing their
poems.excerpt:
They light their own lamps and sing their own words in their temples.
But the birds sing thy name in thine own morning light,—for thy name is joy.

poems.title: Stray Birds 286: Lead me in the centre of thy silence
poems.excerpt: Lead me in the centre of thy silence to fill my heart with songs.

poems.title: Stray Birds 287: Let them live who choose in their own
poems.excerpt:
Let them live who choose in their own hissing world of fireworks.
My heart longs for thy stars, my God.

poems.title: Stray Birds 288: Love's pain sang round my life like the
poems.excerpt: Love's pain sang round my life like the unplumbed sea, and love's joy sang like birds in its flowering groves.

poems.title: Stray Birds 289: Put out the lamp when thou wishest
poems.excerpt:
Put out the lamp when thou wishest.
I shall know thy darkness and shall love it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 290: When I stand before thee at the day's
poems.excerpt: When I stand before thee at the day's end thou shalt see my scars and know that I had my wounds and also my healing.

poems.title: Stray Birds 291: Some day I shall sing to thee in
poems.excerpt: Some day I shall sing to thee in the sunrise of some other world, "I have seen thee before in the light of the earth, in the love of man."

poems.title: Stray Birds 292: Clouds come floating into my life from other
poems.excerpt: Clouds come floating into my life from other days no longer to shed rain or usher storm but to give colour to my sunset sky.

poems.title: Stray Birds 293: Truth raises against itself the storm that scatters
poems.excerpt: Truth raises against itself the storm that scatters its seeds broadcast.

poems.title: Stray Birds 294: The storm of the last night has crowned
poems.excerpt: The storm of the last night has crowned this morning with golden peace.

poems.title: Stray Birds 295: Truth seems to come with its final word
poems.excerpt: Truth seems to come with its final word; and the final word gives birth to its next.

poems.title: Stray Birds 296: Blessed is he whose fame does not outshine
poems.excerpt: Blessed is he whose fame does not outshine his truth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 297: Sweetness of thy name fills my heart when
poems.excerpt: Sweetness of thy name fills my heart when I forget mine—like thy morning sun when the mist is melted.

poems.title: Stray Birds 298: The silent night has the beauty of the
poems.excerpt: The silent night has the beauty of the mother and the clamorous day of the child.

poems.title: Stray Birds 299: The world loved man when he smiled
poems.excerpt: The world loved man when he smiled.  The world became afraid of him when he laughed.

poems.title: Stray Birds 300: God waits for man to regain his childhood
poems.excerpt: God waits for man to regain his childhood in wisdom.

poems.title: Stray Birds 301: Let me feel this world as thy love
poems.excerpt: Let me feel this world as thy love taking form, then my love will help it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 302: Thy sunshine smiles upon the winter days of
poems.excerpt: Thy sunshine smiles upon the winter days of my heart, never doubting of its spring flowers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 303: God kisses the finite in his love and
poems.excerpt: God kisses the finite in his love and man the infinite.

poems.title: Stray Birds 304: Thou crossest desert lands of barren years to
poems.excerpt: Thou crossest desert lands of barren years to reach the moment of fulfilment.

poems.title: Stray Birds 305: God's silence ripens man's thoughts into speech
poems.excerpt: God's silence ripens man's thoughts into speech.

poems.title: Stray Birds 306: Thou wilt find
poems.excerpt: Thou wilt find, Eternal Traveller, marks of thy footsteps across my songs.

poems.title: Stray Birds 307: Let me not shame thee
poems.excerpt: Let me not shame thee, Father, who displayest thy glory in thy children.

poems.title: Stray Birds 308: Cheerless is the day
poems.excerpt: Cheerless is the day, the light under frowning clouds is like a punished child with traces of tears on its pale cheeks, and the cry of the wind is like the cry of a wounded world.  But I know I am travelling to meet my Friend.

poems.title: Stray Birds 309: To-night there is a stir among the palm
poems.excerpt: To-night there is a stir among the palm leaves, a swell in the sea, Full Moon, like the heart throb of the world.  From what unknown sky hast thou carried in thy silence the aching secret of love?

poems.title: Stray Birds 310: I dream of a star
poems.excerpt: I dream of a star, an island of light, where I shall be born and in the depth of its quickening leisure my life will ripen its works like the ricefield in the autumn sun.

poems.title: Stray Birds 311: The smell of the wet earth in the
poems.excerpt: The smell of the wet earth in the rain rises like a great chant of praise from the voiceless multitude of the insignificant.

poems.title: Stray Birds 312: That love can ever lose is a fact
poems.excerpt: That love can ever lose is a fact that we cannot accept as truth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 313: We shall know some day that death can
poems.excerpt: We shall know some day that death can never rob us of that which our soul has gained, for her gains are one with herself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 314: God comes to me in the dusk of
poems.excerpt: God comes to me in the dusk of my evening with the flowers from my past kept fresh in his basket.

poems.title: Stray Birds 315: When all the strings of my life will
poems.excerpt: When all the strings of my life will be tuned, my Master, then at every touch of thine will come out the music of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 316: Let me live truly
poems.excerpt: Let me live truly, my Lord, so that death to me become true.

poems.title: Stray Birds 317: Man's history is waiting in patience for the
poems.excerpt: Man's history is waiting in patience for the triumph of the insulted man.

poems.title: Stray Birds 318: I feel thy gaze upon my heart this
poems.excerpt: I feel thy gaze upon my heart this moment like the sunny silence of the morning upon the lonely field whose harvest is over.

poems.title: Stray Birds 319: I long for the Island of Songs across
poems.excerpt: I long for the Island of Songs across this heaving Sea of Shouts.

poems.title: Stray Birds 320: The prelude of the night is commenced in
poems.excerpt: The prelude of the night is commenced in the music of the sunset, in its solemn hymn to the ineffable dark.

poems.title: Stray Birds 321: I have scaled the peak and found no
poems.excerpt: I have scaled the peak and found no shelter in fame's bleak and barren height.  Lead me, my Guide, before the light fades, into the valley of quiet where life's harvest mellows into golden wisdom.

poems.title: Stray Birds 322: Things look phantastic in this dimness of the
poems.excerpt:
Things look phantastic in this dimness of the dusk—the spires whose bases are lost in the dark and tree tops like blots of ink.
I shall wait for the morning and wake up to see thy city in the light.

poems.title: Stray Birds 323: I have suffered and despaired and known death
poems.excerpt: I have suffered and despaired and known death and I am glad that I am in this great world.

poems.title: Stray Birds 324: There are tracts in my life that are
poems.excerpt: There are tracts in my life that are bare and silent.  They are the open spaces where my busy days had their light and air.

poems.title: Stray Birds 325: Release me from my unfulfilled past clinging to
poems.excerpt: Release me from my unfulfilled past clinging to me from behind making death difficult.

poems.title: Stray Birds 326: Let this be my last word
poems.excerpt: Let this be my last word, that I trust in thy love.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 1: Bid me and I shall gather my fruits
poems.excerpt:
Bid me and I shall gather my fruits to bring them in full baskets into your courtyard, though some are lost and some not ripe.

For the season grows heavy with its fulness, and there is a plaintive shepherd's pipe in the shade. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 2: My life when young was like a flower
poems.excerpt:
My life when young was like a flower—a flower that loosens a petal or two from her abundance and never feels the loss when the spring breeze comes to beg at her door.

Now at the end of youth my life is like a fruit, having nothing to spare, and waiting to offer herself completely with her full burden of sweetness.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 3: Is summer's festival only for fresh blossoms and
poems.excerpt:
Is summer's festival only for fresh blossoms and not also for withered leaves and faded flowers?

Is the song of the sea in tune only with the rising waves? …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 4: I woke and found his letter with the
poems.excerpt:
I woke and found his letter with the morning.

I do not know what it says, for I cannot read. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 5: A handful of dust could hide your signal
poems.excerpt:
A handful of dust could hide your signal when I did not know its meaning.

Now that I am wiser I read it in all that hid it before. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 6: Where roads are made I lose my way
poems.excerpt:
Where roads are made I lose my way.

In the wide water, in the blue sky there is no line of a track. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 7: Alas
poems.excerpt:
Alas, I cannot stay in the house, and home has become no home to me, for the eternal Stranger calls, he is going along the road.

The sound of his footfall knocks at my breast; it pains me! …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 8: Be ready to launch forth
poems.excerpt:
Be ready to launch forth, my heart! and let those linger who must.

For your name has been called in the morning sky. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 9: When I lingered among my hoarded treasure I
poems.excerpt:
When I lingered among my hoarded treasure I felt like a worm that feeds in the dark upon the fruit where it was born.

I leave this prison of decay. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 10: You took my hand and drew me to
poems.excerpt:
You took my hand and drew me to your side, made me sit on the high seat before all men, till I became timid, unable to stir and walk my own way; doubting and debating at every step lest I should tread upon any thorn of their disfavour.

I am freed at last! …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 11: It decks me only to mock me
poems.excerpt:
It decks me only to mock me, this jewelled chain of mine.

It bruises me when on my neck, it strangles me when I struggle to tear it off. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 12: Far below flowed the Jumna
poems.excerpt:
Far below flowed the Jumna, swift and clear, above frowned the jutting bank.

Hills dark with the woods and scarred with the torrents were gathered around. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 13: To move is to meet you every moment
poems.excerpt:
To move is to meet you every moment, Fellow-traveller!

It is to sing to the falling of your feet. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 14: My portion of the best in this world
poems.excerpt:
My portion of the best in this world will come from your hands: such was your promise.

Therefore your light glistens in my tears. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 15: Your speech is simple
poems.excerpt:
Your speech is simple, my Master, but not theirs who talk of you.

I understand the voice of your stars and the silence of your trees. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 16: They knew the way and went to seek
poems.excerpt:
They knew the way and went to seek you along the narrow lane, but I wandered abroad into the night for I was ignorant.

I was not schooled enough to be afraid of you in the dark, therefore I came upon your doorstep unaware. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 17: I brought out my earthen lamp from my
poems.excerpt:
I brought out my earthen lamp from my house and cried, "Come, children, I will light your path!"

The night was still dark when I returned, leaving the road to its silence, crying, "Light me, O Fire! for my earthen lamp lies broken in the dust!"

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 18: No
poems.excerpt:
No: it is not yours to open buds into blossoms.

Shake the bud, strike it; it is beyond your power to make it blossom. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 19: Sudâs
poems.excerpt:
Sudâs, the gardener, plucked from his tank the last lotus left by the ravage of winter and went to sell it to the king at the palace gate.

There he met a traveller who said to him, "Ask your price for the last lotus, —I shall offer it to Lord Buddha." …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 20: Make me thy poet
poems.excerpt:
Make me thy poet, O Night, veiled Night!

There are some who have sat speechless for ages in thy shadow; let me utter their songs. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 21: I will meet one day the Life within
poems.excerpt:
I will meet one day the Life within me, the joy that hides in my life, though the days perplex my path with their idle dust.

I have known it in glimpses, and its fitful breath has come upon me, making my thoughts fragrant for a while. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 22: This autumn morning is tired with excess of
poems.excerpt:
This autumn morning is tired with excess of light, and if your songs grow fitful and languid give me your flute awhile.

I shall but play with it as the whim takes me,—now take it on my lap, now touch it with my lips, now keep it by my side on the grass. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 23: The poet's mind floats and dances on the
poems.excerpt:
The poet's mind floats and dances on the waves of life amidst the voices of wind and water.

Now when the sun has set and the darkened sky draws upon the sea like drooping lashes upon a weary eye it is time to take away his pen, and let his thoughts sink into the bottom of the deep amid the eternal secret of that silence.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 24: The night is dark and your slumber is
poems.excerpt:
The night is dark and your slumber is deep in the hush of my being.

Wake, O Pain of Love, for I know not how to open the door, and I stand outside. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 25: The bird of the morning sings
poems.excerpt:
The bird of the morning sings.

Whence has he word of the morning before the morning breaks, and when the dragon night still holds the sky in its cold black coils? …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 26: The beggar in me lifted his lean hands
poems.excerpt:
The beggar in me lifted his lean hands to the starless sky and cried into night's ear with his hungry voice.

His prayers were to the blind Darkness who lay like a fallen god in a desolate heaven of lost hopes. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 27: Sanâtan was telling his beads by the Ganges
poems.excerpt:
Sanâtan was telling his beads by the Ganges when a Brahmin in rags came to him and said, "Help me, I am poor!"

"My alms-bowl is all that is my own," said Sanâtan, "I have given away everything I had." …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 28: Time after time I came to your gate
poems.excerpt:
Time after time I came to your gate with raised hands, asking for more and yet more.

You gave and gave, now in slow measure, now in sudden excess. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 29: You have set me among those who are
poems.excerpt:
You have set me among those who are defeated.

I know it is not for me to win, nor to leave the game. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 30: A smile of mirth spread over the sky
poems.excerpt:
A smile of mirth spread over the sky when you dressed my heart in rags and sent her forth into the road to beg.

She went from door to door, and many a time when her bowl was nearly full she was robbed. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 31: "Who among you will take up the duty
poems.excerpt:
"Who among you will take up the duty of feeding the hungry?" Lord Buddha asked his followers when famine raged at Shravasti.

Ratnâkar, the banker, hung his head and said, "Much more is needed than all my wealth to feed the hungry." …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 32: My king was unknown to me
poems.excerpt:
My king was unknown to me, therefore when he claimed his tribute I was bold to think I would hide myself leaving my debts unpaid.

I fled and fled behind my day's work and my night's dreams. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 33: When I thought I would mould you
poems.excerpt:
When I thought I would mould you, an image from my life for men to worship, I brought my dust and desires and all my coloured delusions and dreams.

When I asked you to mould with my life an image from your heart for you to love, you brought your fire and force, and truth, loveliness and peace.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 34: "Sire," announced the servant to the King
poems.excerpt:
"Sire," announced the servant to the King, "the saint Narottam has never deigned to enter your royal temple.

"He is singing God's praise under the trees by the open road. The temple is empty of worshippers. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 35: The trumpet lies in the dust
poems.excerpt:
The trumpet lies in the dust.

The wind is weary, the light is dead. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 36: When
poems.excerpt:
When, mad in their mirth, they raised dust to soil thy robe, O Beautiful, it made my heart sick.

I cried to thee and said, "Take thy rod of punishment and judge them." …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 37: Upagupta
poems.excerpt:
Upagupta, the disciple of Buddha, lay asleep on the dust by the city wall of Mathura.

Lamps were all out, doors were all shut, and stars were all hidden by the murky sky of August. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 38: This is no mere dallying of love between
poems.excerpt:
This is no mere dallying of love between us, my lover.

Again and again have swooped down upon me the screaming nights of storm, blowing out my lamp: dark doubts have gathered, blotting out all stars from my sky. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 39: The wall breaks asunder
poems.excerpt:
The wall breaks asunder, light, like divine laughter, bursts in. Victory, O Light!

The heart of the night is pierced! …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 40: O fire
poems.excerpt:
O fire, my brother, I sing victory to you.

You are the bright red image of fearful freedom. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 41: The Boatman is out crossing the wild sea
poems.excerpt:
The Boatman is out crossing the wild sea at night.

The mast is aching because of its full sails filled with the violent wind. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 42: I cling to this living raft
poems.excerpt:
I cling to this living raft, my body, in the narrow stream of my earthly years.

I leave it when the crossing is over.  And then? …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 43: Over the relic of Lord Buddha King Bimbisâr
poems.excerpt:
Over the relic of Lord Buddha King Bimbisâr built a shrine, a salutation in white marble.

There in the evening would come all the brides and daughters of the King's house to offer flowers and light lamps. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 44: The day that stands between you and me
poems.excerpt:
The day that stands between you and me makes her last bow of farewell.

The night draws her veil over her face, and hides the one lamp burning in my chamber. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 45: My night has passed on the bed of
poems.excerpt:
My night has passed on the bed of sorrow, and my eyes are tired. My heavy heart is not yet ready to meet morning with its crowded joys.

Draw a veil over this naked light, beckon aside from me this glaring flash and dance of life. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 46: The time is past when I could repay
poems.excerpt:
The time is past when I could repay her for all that I received.

Her night has found its morning and thou hast taken her to thy arms: and to thee I bring my gratitude and my gifts that were for her. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 47: I found a few old letters of mine
poems.excerpt:
I found a few old letters of mine carefully hidden in her box—a few small toys for her memory to play with.

With a timorous heart she tried to steal these trifles from time's turbulent stream, and said, "These are mine only!" …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 48: Bring beauty and order into my forlorn life
poems.excerpt:
Bring beauty and order into my forlorn life, woman, as you brought them into my house when you lived.

Sweep away the dusty fragments of the hours, fill the empty jars, and mend all that has been neglected. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 49: The pain was great when the strings were
poems.excerpt:
The pain was great when the strings were being tuned, my Master!

Begin your music, and let me forget the pain; let me feel in beauty what you had in your mind through those pitiless days. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 50: In the lightning flash of a moment I
poems.excerpt:
In the lightning flash of a moment I have seen the immensity of your creation in my life—creation through many a death from world to world.

I weep at my unworthiness when I see my life in the hands of the unmeaning hours,—but when I see it in your hands I know it is too precious to be squandered among shadows.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 51: I know that at the dim end of
poems.excerpt:
I know that at the dim end of some day the sun will bid me its farewell.

Shepherds will play their pipes beneath the banyan trees, and cattle graze on the slope by the river, while my days will pass into the dark. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 52: What music is that in whose measure the
poems.excerpt:
What music is that in whose measure the world is rocked?

We laugh when it beats upon the crest of life, we shrink in terror when it returns into the dark. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 53: I have kissed this world with my eyes
poems.excerpt:
I have kissed this world with my eyes and my limbs; I have wrapt it within my heart in numberless folds; I have flooded its days and nights with thoughts till the world and my life have grown one,—and I love my life because I love the light of the sky so enwoven with me.

If to leave this world be as real as to love it—then there must be a meaning in the meeting and the parting of life. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 54: The Cloud said to me
poems.excerpt:
The Cloud said to me, "I vanish"; the Night said, "I plunge into the fiery dawn."

The Pain said, "I remain in deep silence as his footprint." …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 55: Tulsidas
poems.excerpt:
Tulsidas, the poet, was wandering, deep in thought, by the Ganges, in that lonely spot where they burn their dead.

He found a woman sitting at the feet of the corpse of her dead husband, gaily dressed as for a wedding. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 56: You came for a moment to my side
poems.excerpt:
You came for a moment to my side and touched me with the great mystery of the woman that there is in the heart of creation.

She who is ever returning to God his own outflowing of sweetness; she is the ever fresh beauty and youth in nature; she dances in the bubbling streams and sings in the morning light; she with heaving waves suckles the thirsty earth; in her the Eternal One breaks in two in a joy that no longer may contain itself, and overflows in the pain of love.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 57: Who is she who dwells in my heart
poems.excerpt:
Who is she who dwells in my heart, the woman forlorn for ever?

I wooed her and I failed to win her.  I decked her with wreaths and sang in her praise. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 58: Yours is the light that breaks forth from
poems.excerpt:
Yours is the light that breaks forth from the dark, and the good that sprouts from the cleft heart of strife.

Yours is the house that opens upon the world, and the love that calls to the battlefield. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 59: When the weariness of the road is upon
poems.excerpt:
When the weariness of the road is upon me, and the thirst of the sultry day; when the ghostly hours of the dusk throw their shadows across my life, then I cry not for your voice only, my friend, but for your touch.

There is an anguish in my heart for the burden of its riches not given to you. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 60: The odour cries in the bud
poems.excerpt:
The odour cries in the bud, "Ah me, the day departs, the happy day of spring, and I am a prisoner in petals!"

Do not lose heart, timid thing! Your bonds will burst, the bud will open into flower, and when you die in the fulness of life, even then the spring will live on. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 61: She is still a child
poems.excerpt:
She is still a child, my lord.

She runs about your palace and plays, and tries to make of you a plaything as well. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 62: "What is there but the sky
poems.excerpt:
"What is there but the sky, O Sun, that can hold thine image?"

"I dream of thee, but to serve thee I can never hope," the dewdrop wept and said, "I am too small to take thee unto me, great lord, and my life is all tears." …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 63: Not for me is the love that knows
poems.excerpt:
Not for me is the love that knows no restraint, but like the foaming wine that having burst its vessel in a moment would run to waste.

Send me the love which is cool and pure like your rain that blesses the thirsty earth and fills the homely earthen jars. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 64: The sun had set on the western margin
poems.excerpt:
The sun had set on the western margin of the river among the tangle of the forest.

The hermit boys had brought the cattle home, and sat round the fire to listen to the master, Guatama, when a strange boy came, and greeted him with fruits and flowers, and, bowing low at his feet, spoke in a bird-like voice—"Lord, I have come to thee to be taken into the path of the supreme Truth. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 65: May be there is one house in this
poems.excerpt:
May be there is one house in this city where the gate opens for ever this morning at the touch of the sunrise, where the errand of the light is fulfilled.

The flowers have opened in hedges and gardens, and may be there is one heart that has found in them this morning the gift that has been on its voyage from endless time.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 66: Listen
poems.excerpt:
Listen, my heart, in his flute is the music of the smell of wild flowers, of the glistening leaves and gleaming water, of shadows resonant with bees' wings.

The flute steals his smile from my friend's lips and spreads it over my life.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 67: You always stand alone beyond the stream of
poems.excerpt:
You always stand alone beyond the stream of my songs.

The waves of my tunes wash your feet but I know not how to reach them. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 68: Suddenly the window of my heart flew open
poems.excerpt:
Suddenly the window of my heart flew open this morning, the window that looks out on your heart.

I wondered to see that the name by which you know me is written in April leaves and flowers, and I sat silent. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 69: You were in the centre of my heart
poems.excerpt:
You were in the centre of my heart, therefore when my heart wandered she never found you; you hid yourself from my loves and hopes till the last, for you were always in them.

You were the inmost joy in the play of my youth, and when I was too busy with the play the joy was passed by. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 70: When you hold your lamp in the sky
poems.excerpt:
When you hold your lamp in the sky it throws its light on my face and its shadow falls over you.

When I hold the lamp of love in my heart its light falls on you and I am left standing behind in the shadow.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 71: O the waves
poems.excerpt:
O the waves, the sky-devouring waves, glistening with light, dancing with life, the waves of eddying joy, rushing for ever.

The stars rock upon them, thoughts of every tint are cast up out of the deep and scattered on the beach of life. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 72: The joy ran from all the world to
poems.excerpt:
The joy ran from all the world to build my body.

The lights of the skies kissed and kissed her till she woke. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 73: The spring with its leaves and flowers has
poems.excerpt:
The spring with its leaves and flowers has come into my body.

The bees hum there the morning long, and the winds idly play with the shadows. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 74: My bonds are cut
poems.excerpt:
My bonds are cut, my debts are paid, my door has been opened, I go everywhere.

They crouch in their corner and weave their web of pale hours, they count their coins sitting in the dust and call me back. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 75: It was only the other day that I
poems.excerpt:
It was only the other day that I came to your earth, naked and nameless, with a wailing cry.

To-day my voice is glad, while you, my lord, stand aside to make room that I may fill my life. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 76: Timidly I cowered in the shadow of safety
poems.excerpt:
Timidly I cowered in the shadow of safety, but now, when the surge of joy carries my heart upon its crest, my heart clings to the cruel rock of its trouble.

I sat alone in a corner of my house thinking it too narrow for any guest, but now when its door is flung open by an unbidden joy I find there is room for thee and for all the world. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 77: The world is yours at once and for
poems.excerpt:
The world is yours at once and for ever.

And because you have no want, my king, you have no pleasure in your wealth. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 78: To the birds you gave songs
poems.excerpt:
To the birds you gave songs, the birds gave you songs in return.

You gave me only voice, yet asked for more, and I sing. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 79: Let me not pray to be sheltered from
poems.excerpt:
Let me not pray to be sheltered from dangers but to be fearless in facing them.

Let me not beg for the stilling of my pain but for the heart to conquer it. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 80: You did not know yourself when you dwelt
poems.excerpt:
You did not know yourself when you dwelt alone, and there was no crying of an errand when the wind ran from the hither to the farther shore.

I came and you woke, and the skies blossomed with lights. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 81: You
poems.excerpt:
You, in your timeless watch, listen to my approaching steps while your gladness gathers in the morning twilight and breaks in the burst of light.

The nearer I draw to you the deeper grows the fervour in the dance of the sea. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 82: I will utter your name
poems.excerpt:
I will utter your name, sitting alone among the shadows of my silent thoughts.

I will utter it without words, I will utter it without purpose. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 83: I I feel that all the stars shine
poems.excerpt:
I

I feel that all the stars shine in me.  The world breaks into my life like a flood. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 84: The Oarsmen
poems.excerpt:
Do you hear the tumult of death afar, The call midst the fire-floods and poisonous clouds —The Captain's call to the steersman to turn the ship to an unnamed shore, For that time is over—the stagnant time in the port— Where the same old merchandise is bought and sold in an endless round, Where dead things drift in the exhaustion and emptiness of truth.

They wake up in sudden fear and ask, "Comrades, what hour has struck? When shall the dawn begin?" The clouds have blotted away the stars— Who is there then can see the beckoning finger of the day? They run out with oars in hand, the beds are emptied, the mother prays, the wife watches by the door; There is a wail of parting that rises to the sky, And there is the Captain's voice in the dark: "Come, sailors, for the time in the harbour is over!" …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 85: The Song Of The Defeated
poems.excerpt:
My Master has bid me while I stand at the roadside, to sing the song of Defeat, for that is the bride whom He woos in secret.

She has put on the dark veil, hiding her face from the crowd, but the jewel glows on her breast in the dark. …

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 86: Thanksgiving
poems.excerpt:
Those who walk on the path of pride crushing the lowly life under their tread, covering the tender green of the earth with their footprints in blood;

Let them rejoice, and thank thee, Lord, for the day is theirs. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Home
poems.excerpt:
I PACED alone on the road across the field while the sunset was hiding its last gold like a miser.
The daylight sank deeper and deeper into the darkness, and the widowed land, whose harvest had been reaped, lay silent.
Suddenly a boy's shrill voice rose into the sky. He traversed the dark unseen, leaving the track of his song across the hush of the evening. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: On the Seashore
poems.excerpt:
ON the seashore of endless worlds children meet.
The infinite sky is motionless overhead and the restless water is boisterous. On the seashore of endless worlds the children meet with shouts and dances.
 …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Source
poems.excerpt:
The sleep that flits on baby's eyes—does anybody know from where it comes? Yes, there is a rumour that it has its dwelling where, in the fairy village among shadows of the forest dimly lit with glow-worms, there hang two shy buds of enchantment. From there it comes to kiss baby's eyes.
The smile that flickers on baby's lips when he sleeps—does anybody know where it was born? Yes, there is a rumour that a young pale beam of a crescent moon touched the edge of a vanishing autumn cloud, and there the smile was first born in the dream of a dew-washed morning—the smile that flickers on baby's lips when he sleeps.
The sweet, soft freshness that blooms on baby's limbs—does anybody know where it was hidden so long? Yes, when the mother was a young girl it lay pervading her heart in tender and silent mystery of love—the sweet, soft freshness that has bloomed on baby's limbs.

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Baby's Way
poems.excerpt:
If baby only wanted to, he could fly up to heaven this moment.
It is not for nothing that he does not leave us.
He loves to rest his head on mother's bosom, and cannot ever bear to lose sight of her. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Unheeded Pageant
poems.excerpt:
Ah, who was it coloured that little frock, my child, and covered your sweet limbs with that little red tunic?
You have come out in the morning to play in the courtyard, tottering and tumbling as you run.
But who was it coloured that little frock, my child? …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Sleep-Stealer
poems.excerpt:
Who stole sleep from baby's eyes? I must know.
Clasping her pitcher to her waist, mother went to fetch water from the village near by.
It was noon. The children's playtime was over; the ducks in the pond were silent. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Beginning
poems.excerpt:
"Where have I come from, where did you pick me up?" the baby asked its mother.
She answered half crying, half laughing, and clasping the baby to her breast,—
"You were hidden in my heart as its desire, my darling. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Baby's World
poems.excerpt:
I WISH I could take a quiet corner in the heart of my baby's very own world.
I know it has stars that talk to him, and a sky that stoops down to his face to amuse him with its silly clouds and rainbows.
Those who make believe to be dumb, and look as if they never could move, come creeping to his window with their stories and with trays crowded with bright toys. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: When and Why
poems.excerpt:
When I bring you coloured toys, my child, I understand why there is such a play of colours on clouds, on water, and why flowers are painted in tints—when I give coloured toys to you, my child.
When I sing to make you dance, I truly know why there is music in leaves, and why waves send their chorus of voices to the heart of the listening earth—when I sing to make you dance.
When I bring sweet things to your greedy hands, I know why there is honey in the cup of the flower, and why fruits are secretly filled with sweet juice—when I bring sweet things to your greedy hands. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Defamation
poems.excerpt:
Why are those tears in your eyes, my child?
How horrid of them to be always scolding you for nothing!
You have stained your fingers and face with ink while writing—is that why they call you dirty? …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Judge
poems.excerpt:
Say of him what you please, but I know my child's failings.
I do not love him because he is good, but because he is my little child.
How should you know how dear he can be when you try to weigh his merits against his faults? …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Playthings
poems.excerpt:
Child, how happy you are sitting in the dust, playing with a broken twig all the morning.
I smile at your play with that little bit of a broken twig.
I am busy with my accounts, adding up figures by the hour. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Astronomer
poems.excerpt:
I ONLY said, "When in the evening the round full moon gets entangled among the branches of that Kadam tree, couldn't somebody catch it?"
But dādā laughed at me and said, "Baby, you are the silliest child I have ever known. The moon is ever so far from us, how could anybody catch it?"
I said, "Dādā, how foolish you are! When mother looks out of her window and smiles down at us playing, would you call her far away?" …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Clouds and Waves
poems.excerpt:
Mother, the folk who live up in the clouds call out to me—
"We play from the time we wake till the day ends.
We play with the golden dawn, we play with the silver moon." …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Champa Flower
poems.excerpt:
Supposing I became a champa flower, just for fun, and grew on a branch high up that tree, and shook in the wind with laughter and danced upon the newly budded leaves, would you know me, mother?
You would call, "Baby, where are you?" and I should laugh to myself and keep quite quiet.
I should slyly open my petals and watch you at your work. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Fairyland
poems.excerpt:
If people came to know where my king's palace is, it would vanish into the air.
The walls are of white silver and the roof of shining gold.
The queen lives in a palace with seven courtyards, and she wears a jewel that cost all the wealth of seven kingdoms. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Land of the Exile
poems.excerpt:
Mother, the light has grown grey in the sky; I do not know what the time is.
There is no fun in my play, so I have come to you. It is Saturday, our holiday.
Leave off your work, mother; sit here by the window and tell me where the desert of Tepãntar in the fairy tale is? …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Rainy Day
poems.excerpt:
Sullen clouds are gathering fast over the black fringe of the forest.
O child, do not go out!
The palm trees in a row by the lake are smiting their heads against the dismal sky; the crows with their draggled wings are silent on the tamarind branches, and the eastern bank of the river is haunted by a deepening gloom. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Paper Boats
poems.excerpt:
Day by day I float my paper boats one by one down the running stream.
In big black letters I write my name on them and the name of the village where I live.
I hope that someone in some strange land will find them and know who I am. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Sailor
poems.excerpt:
The boat of the boatman Madhu is moored at the wharf of Rajgunj.
It is uselessly laden with jute, and has been lying there idle for ever so long.
If he would only lend me his boat, I should man her with a hundred oars, and hoist sails, five or six or seven. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Further Bank
The Crescent Moon: The Flower-School
poems.excerpt:
When storm clouds rumble in the sky and June showers come down,
The moist east wind comes marching over the heath to blow its bagpipes among the bamboos.
Then crowds of flowers come out of a sudden, from nobody knows where, and dance upon the grass in wild glee. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Merchant
poems.excerpt:
Imagine, mother, that you are to stay at home and I am to travel into strange lands.
Imagine that my boat is ready at the landing fully laden.
Now think well, mother, before you say what I shall bring for you when I come back. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Sympathy
poems.excerpt:
If I were only a little puppy, not your baby, mother dear, would you say "No" to me if I tried to eat from your dish?
Would you drive me off, saying to me, "Get away, you naughty little puppy?"
Then go, mother, go! I will never come to you when you call me, and never let you feed me any more. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Vocation
poems.excerpt:
When the gong sounds ten in the morning and I walk to school by our lane,
Everyday I meet the hawker crying, "Bangles, crystal bangles!"
There is nothing to hurry him on, there is no road he must take, no place he must go to, no time when he must come home. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Superior
poems.excerpt:
Mother, your baby is silly! She is so absurdly childish!
She does not know the difference between the lights in the streets and the stars.
When we play at eating with pebbles, she thinks they are real food, and tries to put them into her mouth. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Little Big Man
poems.excerpt:
I AM small because I am a little child. I shall be big when I am as old as my father is.
My teacher will come and say, "It is late, bring your slate and your books."
I shall tell him, "Do you not know I am as big as father? And I must not have lessons any more." …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Twelve O'clock
poems.excerpt:
Mother, I do want to leave off my lessons now. I have been at my book all the morning.
You say it is only twelve o'clock. Suppose it isn't any later; can't you ever think it is afternoon when it is only twelve o'clock?
I can easily imagine now that the sun has reached the edge of that rice-field, and the old fisher-woman is gathering herbs for her supper by the side of the pond. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Authorship
poems.excerpt:
You say that father writes a lot of books, but what he writes I don't understand.
He was reading to you all the evening, but could you really make out what he meant?
What nice stories, mother, you can tell us! Why can't father write like that, I wonder? …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Wicked Postman
poems.excerpt:
Why do you sit there on the floor so quiet and silent, tell me, mother dear?
The rain is coming in through the open window, making you all wet, and you don't mind it.
Do you hear the gong striking four? It is time for my brother to come home from school. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Hero
poems.excerpt:
Mother, let us imagine we are travelling and passing through a strange and dangerous country.
You are riding in a palanquin and I am trotting by you on a red horse.
It is evening and the sun goes down. The waste of Joradighi lies wan and grey before us. The land is desolate and barren. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The End
poems.excerpt:
It is time for me to go, mother; I am going.
When in the paling darkness of the lonely dawn you stretch out your arms for your baby in the bed, I shall say, "Baby is not there!"—mother, I am going.
I shall become a delicate draught of air and caress you; and I shall be ripples in the water when you bathe, and kiss you and kiss you again. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Recall
poems.excerpt:
The night was dark when she went away, and they slept.
The night is dark now, and I call for her, "Come back, my darling; the world is asleep; and no one would know, if you came for a moment while stars are gazing at stars."
 …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The First Jasmines
poems.excerpt:
Ah, these jasmines, these white jasmines!
I seem to remember the first day when I filled my hands with these jasmines, these white jasmines.
I have loved the sunlight, the sky and the green earth; …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Banyan Tree
poems.excerpt:
O YOU shaggy-headed banyan tree standing on the bank of the pond, have you forgotten the little child, like the birds that have nested in your branches and left you?
Do you not remember how he sat at the window and wondered at the tangle of your roots that plunged underground?
The women would come to fill their jars in the pond, and your huge black shadow would wriggle on the water like sleep struggling to wake up. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: Benediction
poems.excerpt:
Bless this little heart, this white soul that has won the kiss of heaven for our earth.
He loves the light of the sun, he loves the sight of his mother's face.
He has not learned to despise the dust, and to hanker after gold. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Gift
poems.excerpt:
I WANT to give you something, my child, for we are drifting in the stream of the world.
Our lives will be carried apart, and our love forgotten.
But I am not so foolish as to hope that I could buy your heart with my gifts. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: My Song
poems.excerpt:
This song of mine will wind its music around you, my child, like the fond arms of love.
This song of mine will touch your forehead like a kiss of blessing.
When you are alone it will sit by your side and whisper in your ear, when you are in the crowd it will fence you about with aloofness. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Child-Angel
poems.excerpt:
They clamour and fight, they doubt and despair, they know no end to their wranglings.
Let your life come amongst them like a flame of light, my child, unflickering and pure, and delight them into silence.
They are cruel in their greed and their envy, their words are like hidden knives thirsting for blood. …

poems.title: The Crescent Moon: The Last Bargain
poems.excerpt:
"Come and hire me," I cried, while in the morning I was walking on the stone-paved road.
Sword in hand, the King came in his chariot.
He held my hand and said, "I will hire you with my power." …

poems.title: Lover's Gift 1: You allowed your kingly power to vanish
poems.excerpt:
You allowed your kingly power to vanish, Shajahan, but your wish was to make imperishable a tear-drop of love. Time has no pity for the human heart, he laughs at its sad struggle to remember.

You allured him with beauty, made him captive, and crowned the formless death with fadeless form. …

poems.title: Lover's Gift 2: Come to my garden walk
poems.excerpt:
Come to my garden walk, my love. Pass by the fervid flowers that press themselves on your sight. Pass them by, stopping at some chance joy, which like a sudden wonder of sunset illumines, yet eludes.

For love's gift is shy, it never tells its name, it flits across the shade, spreading a shiver of joy along the dust. Overtake it or miss it for ever. But a gift that can be grasped is merely a frail flower, or a lamp with a flame that will flicker.

poems.title: Lover's Gift 3: The fruits come in crowds into my orchard
poems.excerpt:
The fruits come in crowds into my orchard, they jostle each other. They surge up in the light in an anguish of fullness.

Proudly step into my orchard, my queen, sit there in the shade, pluck the ripe fruits from their stems, and let them yield, to the utmost, their burden of sweetness at your lips. …

poems.title: Lover's Gift 4: She is near to my heart as the
poems.excerpt: She is near to my heart as the meadow-flower to the earth; she is sweet to me as sleep is to tired limbs. My love for her is my life flowing in its fullness, like a river in autumn flood, running with serene abandonment. My songs are one with my love, like the murmur of a stream, that sings with all its waves and currents.

poems.title: Lover's Gift 5: I would ask for still more
poems.excerpt: I would ask for still more, if I had the sky with all its stars, and the world with its endless riches; but I would be content with the smallest corner of this earth if only she were mine.

poems.title: Lover's Gift 6: In the light of this thriftless day of
poems.excerpt:
In the light of this thriftless day of spring, my poet, sing of those who pass by and do not linger, who laugh as they run and never look back, who blossom in an hour of unreasoning delight, and fade in a moment without regret.

Do not sit down silently, to tell the beads of your past tears and smiles,—do not stop to pick up the dropped petals from the flowers of overnight, do not go to seek things that evade you, to know the meaning that is not plain,—leave the gaps in your life where they are, for the music to come out of their depths.

poems.title: Lover's Gift 7: It is little that remains now
poems.excerpt:
It is little that remains now, the rest was spent in one careless summer. It is just enough to put in a song and sing to you; to weave in a flower-chain gently clasping your wrist; to hang in your ear like a round pink pearl, like a blushing whisper; to risk in a game one evening and utterly lose.

My boat is a frail small thing, not fit for crossing wild waves in the rain. If you but lightly step on it I shall gently row you by the shelter of the shore, where the dark water in ripples is like a dream-ruffled sleep; where the dove's cooing from the drooping branches makes the noon-day shadows plaintive. At the day's end, when you are tired, I shall pluck a dripping lily to put in your hair and take my leave.

poems.title: Lover's Gift 8: There is room for you
poems.excerpt:
There is room for you. You are alone with your few sheaves of rice. My boat is crowded, it is heavily laden, but how can I turn you away? your young body is slim and swaying; there is a twinkling smile in the edge of your eyes, and your robe is coloured like the rain-cloud.

The travellers will land for different roads and homes. You will sit for a while on the prow of my boat, and at the journey's end none will keep you back. …

poems.title: Lover's Gift 9: Woman, your basket is heavy
poems.excerpt:
Woman, your basket is heavy, your limbs are tired. For what distance have you set out, with what hunger of profit? The way is long and the dust is hot in the sun.

See, the lake is deep and full, its water dark like a crow's eye. The banks are sloping and tender with grass. …

poems.title: Lover's Gift 10: What is it that drives these bees from
poems.excerpt: What is it that drives these bees from their home; these followers of unseen trails? What cry is this in their eager wings? How can they hear the music that sleeps in the flower soul? How can they find their way to the chamber where the honey lies shy and silent?

poems.title: Lover's Gift 11: It was only the budding of leaves in
poems.excerpt:
It was only the budding of leaves in the summer, the summer that came into the garden by the sea. It was only a stir and rustle in the south wind, a few lazy snatches of songs, and then the day was done.

But let there be flowering of love in the summer to come in the garden by the sea. Let my joy take its birth and clap its hands and dance with the surging songs, and make the morning open its eyes wide in sweet amazement.

poems.title: Lover's Gift 12: Ages ago when you opened the south gate
poems.excerpt:
Ages ago when you opened the south gate of the garden of gods, and came down upon the first youth of the earth, O Spring; men and women rushed out of their houses, laughing and dancing, and pelting each other with flower-dust in a sudden madness of mirth

Year after year you bring the same flowers that you scattered in your path in that earliest April. Therefore, to-day, in their pervading perfume, they breathe the sigh of the days that are now dreams,—the clinging sadness of vanished worlds. Your breeze is laden with love-legends that have faded from all human language. …

poems.title: Lover's Gift 13: Last night in the garden I offered you
poems.excerpt:
Last night in the garden I offered you my youth's foaming wine. You lifted the cup to your lips, you shut your eyes and smiled while I raised your veil, unbound your tresses, drawing down upon my breast your face sweet with its silence, last night when the moon's dream overflowed the world of slumber.

To-day in the dew-cooled calm of the dawn you are walking to God's temple, bathed and robed in white, with a basketful of flowers in your hand. I stand aside in the shade under the tree, with my head bent, in the calm of the dawn by the lonely road to the temple.

poems.title: Lover's Gift 14: If I am impatient to-day
poems.excerpt:
If I am impatient to-day, forgive me, my love. It is the first summer rain, and the riverside forest is aflutter, and the blossoming kadam trees, are tempting the passing winds with winecups of perfume. See, from all corners of the sky lightnings are darting their glances, and winds are rampant in your hair.

If to-day I bring my homage to you, forgive me, my love. The everyday world is hidden in the dimness of the rain, all work has stopped in the village, the meadows are desolate. In your dark eyes the coming of the rain finds its music, and it is at your door that July waits with jasmines for your hair in its blue skirt.

poems.title: Lover's Gift 15: Her neighbours call her dark in the village—but
poems.excerpt:
Her neighbours call her dark in the village—but she is a lily to my heart, yes, a lily though not fair. Light came muffled with clouds, when first I saw her in the field; her head was bare, her veil was off, her braided hair hanging loose on her neck. She may be dark as they say in the village, but I have seen her black eyes and am glad.

The pulse of the air boded storm. She rushed out of the hut, when she heard her dappled cow low in dismay. For a moment she turned her large eyes to the clouds, and felt a stir of the coming rain in the sky.
